docs.text: Mazduino Core ¶ Overview ¶ The Mazduino Core is a new-generation ECU built on a 48-pin automotive connector, with a more complete I/O architecture than the Mini 6CH line. It uses an ARM Cortex-M4 180 MHz as its main MCU for advanced engine control, including support for dual ETB , dual CAN bus , combined Hall + VR inputs, and more actuator outputs for modern engines. This documentation is based on the Mazduino Core product specification and the hardware reference in the MAZDUINO CORE document. Key Features ¶ ARM Cortex-M4 180 MHz MCU Built-in 5V sensor supply with internal protection 4x Hall/Digital inputs for CKP, CMP, VSS, clutch, launch, or other switches 12x analog inputs for MAP, TPS, O2, pressure, temperature, PPS, and additional sensors 6x ignition outputs (for smart coils, 5V/12V depending on configuration) 10x 3A low side outputs for injectors, idle PWM, boost, VVT, and medium-load actuators 5x low current low side outputs for relays (main relay, fuel pump, fan, AC, tach) 2x 1.3A high side outputs for 12V switching loads Example uses: alternator control , 12V solenoids, and other switching actuators within the current limit. 2x CAN bus (depending on trace/jumper configuration) 2x VR inputs for variable reluctor CKP/CMP sensors 2x ETB outputs (ETB1 and ETB2) Dual ETB IC (ETB1 and ETB2) can also be used for Idle Stepper control USB, Serial, and CAN communication Firmware support for rusEFI based firmware only (official or custom firmware for the F4 MCU) Hardware and Jumper Configuration ¶ The Mazduino Core has several pins whose function can be switched with solder jumpers. This lets one board be used for many different engine configurations. Solder Jumper Positions JP3, JP4, and JP5 ¶ The JP3 , JP4 , and JP5 solder jumpers are on the bottom of the board. On the back of the board there are jumpers that can be set to suit your needs, or as requested when you order: whether the board will be used on a 6-cylinder or only a 4-cylinder car, or whether you need extra analog inputs or a high side output (12v switching). On JP3, JP4 and JP5, solder the jumper across 2 pins toward the center to pass the signal through to the ECU connector. Solderless Pin Header Jumpers ¶ The solderless pin header jumpers are set as requested when you order, or you can move them yourself as needed. The ECU connector will then carry CANL or VR2-, Digital 4 or VR1-, CANH or VR2+, Digital 3 or VR1+. Additional Pin Headers (Prototype) ¶ For prototyping, there are 4 six-pin headers that accept JST XH 2.54 connectors. Header Pinout J2 5V, Analog Temp 4, Analog Volt 2, Analog Volt 3, GND, GND J5 12V, CANL1, CANH1, CANL2, CANH2, GND J6 5V, 5V, 5V, USB D-, USB D+, GND J7 3.3V, 3.3V, 3.3V, 3.3V, GND Ignition Volt Drive Jumper (12V / 5V) ¶ The Ignition Volt Drive jumper selects the voltage level of the coil trigger signal: 12V or 5V . Be careful and make sure the coil signal voltage is correct. If the voltage level is wrong, the coil can be damaged beyond use. ETB and Idle Stepper Notes ¶ Because there are dual ICs for ETB1 and ETB2 control, those driver channels can also be used for Idle Stepper control, depending on the firmware configuration and wiring. Important Jumper Options ¶ JP3 (Pin 4) : select AVS2 (Analog Volt 5) or Ignition 6 JP4 (Pin 20) : select ATS2 (Analog Temp 4) or Ignition 5 JP5 (Pin 5) : select AVS3 (Analog Volt 6) or High Side 2 IN22 : select Digital 3 or VR1+ IN38 : select Digital 4 or VR1- IN33 : select CANH1 or VR2+ IN34 : select CANL1 or VR2- Configuration Notes ¶ For a full 6-ignition setup, enable ignition mode on Pin 4 and Pin 20. For a setup that needs extra analog inputs, enable analog mode on Pin 4/5/20. For VR trigger sensors, switch the Digital 3/4 or CANH/CANL channels to VR as needed. Always switch off ECU power before changing the jumper configuration. ETB Output 2 sets ETB1 (+/-), ETB2 (+/-) CAN Bus 2 CAN1 via jumper pins; CAN2 depending on board/firmware configuration Firmware Function Mapping ¶ Below is a typical function mapping for the firmware setup. The assignment can be adapted to the engine and the tuning strategy. Typical Function Default Channel Ignition 1-6 Ign 1 to Ign 6 Injector 1-10 Low Side 1 to Low Side 10 Main Relay / Fuel Pump / Fan / AC / Tacho Low Side Low Current 11 to 15 MAP / TPS / O2 / PPS / Pressure sensors Analog Volt 1 to 8 CLT / IAT / Additional temp Analog Temp 1 to 4 CKP / CMP Hall Digital 1 and Digital 2 CKP / CMP VR VR1 and VR2 (via jumper configuration) ETB1 ETB1+ and ETB1- ETB2 ETB2+ and ETB2- MCU Information ¶ MCU : ARM Cortex-M4 180 MHz In the firmware, the ETB control lines are usually mapped to dedicated MCU pins (DIR/DIS/PWM) according to the firmware package. Use the firmware configuration file made specifically for the Mazduino Core so that all pins work as the board was designed. Firmware for this board is rusEFI based only (either official or custom firmware for the F4 MCU). Quick Installation Guide ¶ Make sure all main grounds (pins 17/18/39/40) are well connected. Connect pin 1 to a stable 12V ECU supply. Configure the jumpers before fitting the ECU to the final harness. Select Hall or VR trigger mode according to the CKP/CMP sensor type. If you use 6 ignition channels, enable the ignition option on the related jumper pins. If you use dual ETB, verify the ETB1 and ETB2 wiring and calibrate TPS/PPS. Check the outputs with test mode in TunerStudio/rusEFI before starting the engine. Important Notes ¶ The ignition outputs are intended for smart coils . Dumb coils require an external driver/IGBT. The low current outputs are for relays or light loads, not for driving motors directly. HS1 and HS2 can be used as 12V switching outputs, for example for alternator control . Make sure the Ignition Volt Drive setting (12V/5V) matches the coil specification before powering up the system. All jumper changes must be made with the ECU unpowered . To use CAN2 , follow the hardware schematic and the firmware configuration for your board revision. Software Tuning ¶ Download TunerStudio: TunerStudio Downloads rusEFI firmware reference: wiki.rusefi.com Product information: www.mazduino.com

docs.text: Mazduino Core Rev1 ¶ Overview ¶ The Mazduino Core Rev1 is the follow-up revision of the Mazduino Core Rev0 , an ECU built on a 48-pin automotive connector with a more complete I/O architecture than the Mini 6CH line. It uses an ARM Cortex-M4 180 MHz as its main MCU for advanced engine control, including support for dual ETB , dual CAN bus , combined Hall + VR inputs, and more actuator outputs for modern engines. Rev1 brings several improvements over Rev0, including a new 12V Out sensor supply (pin 17, for example for CKP/CMP sensors that need 12V power), an improved 5V sensor supply that now delivers up to 3A without running hot, named optional jumper channels (CON21, CON22, CON37, CON38), and new jumper options on pin 21 and pin 37. See Changes in Rev1 for the full summary. This documentation is based on the Mazduino Core product specification and the hardware reference in the MAZDUINO CORE document. Key Features ¶ ARM Cortex-M4 180 MHz MCU Built-in 5V sensor supply up to 3A with internal protection, more heat tolerant than Rev0 Built-in 12V sensor supply (pin 17) for sensors that need 12V power, for example 12V-type CKP/CMP sensors 4x Hall/Digital inputs for CKP, CMP, VSS, clutch, launch, or other switches (all with an alternative jumper option) 11x analog inputs for MAP, TPS, O2, pressure, temperature, PPS, and additional sensors 6x ignition outputs (for smart coils, 5V/12V depending on configuration) 10x 3A low side outputs for injectors, idle PWM, boost, VVT, and medium-load actuators 5x low current low side outputs for relays (main relay, fuel pump, fan, AC, tach) 2x 1.3A high side outputs for 12V switching loads Example uses: alternator control , 12V solenoids, and other switching actuators within the current limit. 2x CAN bus (depending on trace/jumper configuration) 2x VR inputs for variable reluctor CKP/CMP sensors 2x ETB outputs (ETB1 and ETB2) Dual ETB IC (ETB1 and ETB2) can also be used for Idle Stepper control USB, Serial, and CAN communication Firmware support for rusEFI based firmware only (official or custom firmware for the F4 MCU) Changes in Rev1 ¶ Compared with Rev0, Rev1 has the following fixes and changes: Pin Rev0 Rev1 Notes 4 (JP3) AVS2 (Analog Volt 5) or Ignition 6 AVS5 (Analog Volt 5) or Ignition 6 Jumper option renamed; the signal is still Analog Volt 5 5 (JP5) AVS3 (Analog Volt 6) or High Side 2 AVS6 (Analog Volt 6) or High Side 2 Jumper option renamed; the signal is still Analog Volt 6 6 5V Sensor Supply 5V Sensor Supply (up to 3A ) Higher 5V supply current capacity, more heat tolerant than Rev0 17 Ground (Power ground) 12V Out (Sensor 12V power) New pin for 12V sensor supply, for example 12V-type CKP/CMP sensors; no longer ground 20 (JP4) ATS2 (Analog Temp 4) or Ignition 5 ATS4 (Analog Temp 4) or Ignition 5 Jumper option renamed; the signal is still Analog Temp 4 21 Digital 1 (fixed) CON21 : Digital 1 or AV5 (Analog Volt 5) — Jumper Option Pin 21 now has an extra jumper option to Analog Volt 5 22 IN22: Digital 3 or VR1+ CON22 : Digital 3 or VR1+ Pin renamed; function unchanged 37 Digital 2 (fixed) CON37 : Digital 2 or AVS6 (Analog Volt 6) — Jumper Option Pin 37 now has an extra jumper option to Analog Volt 6 38 IN38: Digital 4 or VR1- CON38 : Digital 4 or VR1- — Jumper Option Pin renamed; function unchanged 41 Analog Volt 8 Analog Volt 5 The Analog Volt 8 channel was removed; pin 41 now carries Analog Volt 5 directly Caution: On Rev1, pin 17 changes from Ground to 12V Out (12V supply for sensors). Do not wire pin 17 as ground when moving a harness from Rev0 to Rev1. Use pin 18, 39, or 40 for ground. Hardware and Jumper Configuration ¶ The Mazduino Core has several pins whose function can be switched with solder jumpers. This lets one board be used for many different engine configurations. Solder Jumper Positions JP3, JP4, and JP5 ¶ The JP3 , JP4 , and JP5 solder jumpers are on the bottom of the board. On the back of the board there are jumpers that can be set to suit your needs, or as requested when you order: whether the board will be used on a 6-cylinder or only a 4-cylinder car, or whether you need extra analog inputs or a high side output (12v switching). On JP3, JP4 and JP5, solder the jumper across 2 pins toward the center to pass the signal through to the ECU connector. Solderless Pin Header Jumpers ¶ The solderless pin header jumpers are set as requested when you order, or you can move them yourself as needed. The ECU connector will then carry CANL or VR2-, Digital 4 or VR1-, CANH or VR2+, Digital 3 or VR1+ (pins IN33/IN34/CON22/CON38). In addition, on Rev1 the CON21 (Digital 1 or AV5) and CON37 (Digital 2 or AVS6) pins use the same type of solderless pin header jumper. Additional Pin Headers (Prototype) ¶ For prototyping, there are 4 six-pin headers that accept JST XH 2.54 connectors. Header Pinout J2 5V, Analog Temp 4, Analog Volt 2, Analog Volt 3, GND, GND J5 12V, CANL1, CANH1, CANL2, CANH2, GND J6 5V, 5V, 5V, USB D-, USB D+, GND J7 3.3V, 3.3V, 3.3V, 3.3V, GND Ignition Volt Drive Jumper (12V / 5V) ¶ The Ignition Volt Drive jumper selects the voltage level of the coil trigger signal: 12V or 5V . Be careful and make sure the coil signal voltage is correct. If the voltage level is wrong, the coil can be damaged beyond use. ETB and Idle Stepper Notes ¶ Because there are dual ICs for ETB1 and ETB2 control, those driver channels can also be used for Idle Stepper control, depending on the firmware configuration and wiring. Important Jumper Options ¶ JP3 (Pin 4) : select AVS5 (Analog Volt 5) or Ignition 6 JP4 (Pin 20) : select ATS4 (Analog Temp 4) or Ignition 5 JP5 (Pin 5) : select AVS6 (Analog Volt 6) or High Side 2 CON21 (Pin 21) : select Digital 1 or AV5 (Analog Volt 5) CON22 (Pin 22) : select Digital 3 or VR1+ CON37 (Pin 37) : select Digital 2 or AVS6 (Analog Volt 6) CON38 (Pin 38) : select Digital 4 or VR1- IN33 (Pin 33) : select CANH1 or VR2+ IN34 (Pin 34) : select CANL1 or VR2- Configuration Notes ¶ For a full 6-ignition setup, enable ignition mode on Pin 4 and Pin 20. For a setup that needs extra analog inputs, enable analog mode on Pin 4/5/20/21/37. For VR trigger sensors, switch the Digital 3/4 or CANH/CANL channels to VR as needed. Always switch off ECU power before changing the jumper configuration. Typical Function Default Channel Ignition 1-6 Ign 1 to Ign 6 Injector 1-10 Low Side 1 to Low Side 10 Main Relay / Fuel Pump / Fan / AC / Tacho Low Side Low Current 11 to 15 MAP / TPS / O2 / PPS / Pressure sensors Analog Volt 1 to 7 CLT / IAT / Additional temp Analog Temp 1 to 4 CKP / CMP Hall Digital 1 and Digital 2 CKP / CMP VR VR1 and VR2 (via jumper configuration) ETB1 ETB1+ and ETB1- ETB2 ETB2+ and ETB2- Example I/O Usage Scenarios ¶ The Low Side, Analog Volt, and Analog Temp channels are generic, so how they are allocated depends on the engine configuration and the ignition mode used. Some example scenarios: Low Side as injectors : Low Side 1 to 8 can be used as injector outputs for an 8-cylinder full sequential engine (1 injector per channel). For engines with fewer cylinders, or in batch/semi-sequential mode, the number of Low Side channels used for injectors changes accordingly (the rest are free for idle PWM, boost, VVT, or other actuators). Wasted Spark ignition mode : used for engines with 8 cylinders or more , with 4 ignition channels (each coil serves a pair of cylinders). For engines with 6 cylinders or fewer , ignition can be wired individually/COP (1 channel per cylinder) because the board provides up to 6 ignition channels. Unused ignition channels can be switched by jumper (Pin 4/Pin 20) to Analog Volt 5 / Analog Temp 4 for additional sensors. Analog Volt : used for 0-5V analog sensor inputs such as MAP , TPS , O2/wideband , PPS , or other pressure sensors. Analog Temp : used for temperature sensor inputs such as CLT (Coolant Temp) and IAT (Intake Air Temp) . MCU Information ¶ MCU : ARM Cortex-M4 180 MHz In the firmware, the ETB control lines are usually mapped to dedicated MCU pins (DIR/DIS/PWM) according to the firmware package. Use the firmware configuration file made specifically for the Mazduino Core Rev1 so that all pins work as the board was designed. Firmware for this board is rusEFI based only (either official or custom firmware for the F4 MCU). Quick Installation Guide ¶ Make sure all main grounds (pins 18/39/40) are well connected. Connect pin 1 to a stable 12V ECU supply. If you need a 12V supply for sensors (for example 12V-type CKP/CMP sensors), use pin 17 ( 12V Out ). Do not wire it as ground. Configure the jumpers before fitting the ECU to the final harness. Select Hall or VR trigger mode according to the CKP/CMP sensor type. If you use 6 ignition channels, enable the ignition option on the related jumper pins. If you use dual ETB, verify the ETB1 and ETB2 wiring and calibrate TPS/PPS. Check the outputs with test mode in TunerStudio/rusEFI before starting the engine. Important Notes ¶ Pin 17 has a different function than on Rev0 : it changed from Ground to 12V Out (12V supply for sensors, for example 12V-type CKP/CMP). Recheck the harness when moving from Rev0 to Rev1. The 5V Sensor Supply (pin 6) on Rev1 delivers up to 3A and is more heat tolerant than on Rev0, so it is safer when powering many 5V sensors at once. The ignition outputs are intended for smart coils . Dumb coils require an external driver/IGBT. The low current outputs are for relays or light loads, not for driving motors directly. HS1 and HS2 can be used as 12V switching outputs, for example for alternator control . Make sure the Ignition Volt Drive setting (12V/5V) matches the coil specification before powering up the system. All jumper changes must be made with the ECU unpowered . To use CAN2 , follow the hardware schematic and the firmware configuration for your board revision. docs.text: The Mazduino Core Rev1 is the follow-up revision of the Mazduino Core Rev0 , an ECU built on a 48-pin automotive connector with a more complete I/O architecture than the Mini 6CH line. It uses an ARM Cortex-M4 180 MHz as its main MCU for advanced engine control, including support for dual ETB , dual CAN bus , combined Hall + VR inputs, and more actuator outputs for modern engines. Rev1 brings several improvements over Rev0, including a new 12V Out sensor supply (pin 17, for example for CKP/CMP sensors that need 12V power), an improved 5V sensor supply that now delivers up to 3A without running hot, named optional jumper channels (CON21, CON22, CON37, CON38), and new jumper options on pin 21 and pin 37. See Changes in Rev1 for the full summary. This documentation is based on the Mazduino Core product specification and the hardware reference in the MAZDUINO CORE document.
docs.title: Overview

docs.text: ARM Cortex-M4 180 MHz MCU Built-in 5V sensor supply up to 3A with internal protection, more heat tolerant than Rev0 Built-in 12V sensor supply (pin 17) for sensors that need 12V power, for example 12V-type CKP/CMP sensors 4x Hall/Digital inputs for CKP, CMP, VSS, clutch, launch, or other switches (all with an alternative jumper option) 11x analog inputs for MAP, TPS, O2, pressure, temperature, PPS, and additional sensors 6x ignition outputs (for smart coils, 5V/12V depending on configuration) 10x 3A low side outputs for injectors, idle PWM, boost, VVT, and medium-load actuators 5x low current low side outputs for relays (main relay, fuel pump, fan, AC, tach) 2x 1.3A high side outputs for 12V switching loads Example uses: alternator control , 12V solenoids, and other switching actuators within the current limit. 2x CAN bus (depending on trace/jumper configuration) 2x VR inputs for variable reluctor CKP/CMP sensors 2x ETB outputs (ETB1 and ETB2) Dual ETB IC (ETB1 and ETB2) can also be used for Idle Stepper control USB, Serial, and CAN communication Firmware support for rusEFI based firmware only (official or custom firmware for the F4 MCU)

docs.text: Mazduino Dash R4 ¶ Overview ¶ Some Dash R4 themes: Street (default), Wangan Night, Classic Beetle, Motorsport, Car Status, Retro VFD, Synthwave, Halo, Ink Wave, and Classic Mazduino Dash R4 is a round 4 inch dash display with a touch screen. What it shows comes as themes , which you can install, remove, and adjust yourself from the DashTune app over Bluetooth. The choices range from racing gauges and classic gauges to themes with a photo of your own car. Variant Screen Size Connector Dash R4 4 inch, round DTM4 (Deutsch DTM 4 Pin) Key Features ¶ Dozens of ready-to-install themes from the Theme Store in DashTune, with up to 10 themes stored on the dash at once. The Street theme is built into the firmware and is always there. You can change what each data panel in a theme shows, for example from Oil Pressure to IAT. Supports rusEFI , Haltech , MaxxECU , ECUMASTER EMU Black , Link Generic Dash , Speeduino , OBD-II , and M-Link ( CAN IO Extender ). Fuel consumption (km/l) is calculated on the dash, if the ECU sends fuel flow and speed data. Warnings (alarms) for Oil Pressure, Fuel Pressure, CLT, Oil Temp, Fuel Level, and Battery. Extra inputs : turn signal, head light, and fuel level signals can be taken from the car, and the screen dims automatically when the lights are on. The head light input can also be used for a theme change button. Google Maps directions and music from your phone show up as short notifications on the screen. Your own splash screen at power-up, which can be animated, or made from a GIF or video. Firmware updates through the app, with no cable. DTM4 / 4 Pin Connector ¶ Dash R4 uses the same DTM4 (Deutsch DTM 4 Pin) connector as Racedash Pro , both in physical form and in the function of each pin. A cable from a Racedash Pro can be used as is. Dash connector side Cable connector side Pin No. Description 1 12V Power Supply 2 Ground 3 CAN High / TX 4 CAN Low / RX Note: Pins 3 and 4 work as CAN High/CAN Low for all ECUs that use CAN Bus (rusEFI, Haltech, MaxxECU, ECUMASTER, Link, OBD-II, M-Link). For Speeduino ECUs only, pins 3 and 4 work as Serial TX/RX , because Speeduino has no native CAN Bus. Supported ECUs ¶ ECU Connection rusEFI CAN Bus 500 kbps Haltech CAN Bus 1 Mbps MaxxECU CAN Bus 500 kbps ECUMASTER EMU Black CAN Bus 1 Mbps Link Generic Dash CAN Bus 1 Mbps Speeduino Serial OBD-II CAN Bus (ISO 15765-4) M-Link (CAN IO Extender) CAN Bus 500 kbps The ECU type is selected from the menu on the dash screen ( Settings → ECU ) or from DashTune ( General Setting ). No firmware change is needed , and the CAN speed adjusts by itself. Switching between ECUs that both use CAN Bus takes effect immediately, without a restart. Switching from or to Speeduino only takes effect after the dash is turned off and on again, because the function of pins 3 and 4 changes too. What must be enabled on each ECU is covered in ECU Configuration for Racedash . The settings are the same for Dash R4. OBD-II : not every OBD-II car can be read, and the data depends on what your car answers. The limits are the same as on Racedash Pro; read OBD-II limitations before buying for OBD-II use. Themes ¶ A theme is the look of the dashboard. Each theme carries its own gauge layout, colors, and images, like the examples in the Overview . The full list is in the DashTune Theme Store , and new themes keep being added. Switching themes ¶ Swipe left or right on the screen to move to the next theme. Or open the dash menu, choose Themes , then tap the theme you want. The dash remembers the last theme shown. If you want the dash to always start with a particular theme, open Themes in the dash menu and press Set default on that theme. Installing themes from DashTune ¶ Connect DashTune to the dash (see Connecting for the first time ). Open the Themes menu. It shows the themes already installed on the dash, with their images, and how many there are (for example "4 of 10 themes on the dash"). Open the Theme Store , choose a theme, then press download. The theme is sent to the dash over the dash's WiFi. This runs by itself, so keep the phone screen on and do not close the app until it finishes. The dash stores at most 10 themes . When it is full, DashTune asks which theme to remove to make room for the new one. A removed theme stays in the Theme Store and can be installed again at any time. If an installed theme has a newer version in the store, DashTune marks it with UPDATE . Adjusting a theme (Customize) ¶ In the Themes menu, choose an installed theme and press Customize . What can be adjusted differs per theme: Data panel contents : the panels are named Data 1 , Data 2 , and so on. Choose the data to show in that panel, for example Oil Pressure, Fuel Pressure, CLT, IAT, AFR, Battery, or KM/L. Car photo (Car Status theme): replace the default car photo with a photo of your own car. Text (for example the Ink Wave and Sticker Bomb themes): replace the text on the theme with the name of your car or team. Colors and other options the theme provides. Changes are sent to the dash and stay saved even when the dash is turned off. Using a photo of your own car (Car Status) ¶ In Customize , choose Change photo , then Take a photo or Choose from gallery . A photo of the car from the front side gives the best result. Choose how to handle the photo background : Automatic : the app cuts the car out of its background by itself. Manual : erase the background with your finger, using the Erase , Restore , and Undo buttons. Keep : the photo is used as it is, background included. Drag and pinch the photo so the car fits inside the frame. The frame shows the area that appears on the dash. Tap the lights you are asked for (for example the headlights), following the Example below the frame. This tells the dash where the lights are that light up with data from the ECU. Press Save to send the photo to the dash. Dash screen menu ¶ Screen gestures ¶ Gesture Result Swipe left / right Change theme Swipe up from the bottom of the screen Open the menu Swipe down Close the menu Tap the warning banner Silence that warning for 60 seconds Tap the splash screen Skip the splash, go straight to the dashboard The way to open the menu can be changed to Double tap in Settings → Open menu . Menu layout ¶ MENU ├── Settings → Brightness, ECU, Max RPM, Shift RPM, Fuel tank, Open menu ├── Themes → list of themes; tap to show one, Set default for the theme at power-up └── Music → song playing on the phone, with previous / play-pause / next buttons Settings ¶ Setting Function Brightness Screen brightness, 20–100% ECU ECU type / protocol Max RPM Full RPM scale, in steps of 500 RPM Shift RPM RPM at which the shift light starts to light Fuel tank Tank capacity in liters, to calculate the remaining fuel Open menu How to open the menu: Swipe up or Double tap These values are the same ones set in DashTune General Setting , and are saved when the menu is closed ( Done ). Warnings (alarms) ¶ When a value stays past its limit for more than 1 second, a warning banner appears at the bottom of the screen for 6 seconds. The theme stays visible above it. After that the banner goes away for 20 seconds so it does not cover the display, then appears again if the problem is still there. When there are several warnings at once, the banners take turns. Data Default limit Oil Pressure Below 1.0 bar with the engine above 1200 RPM Fuel Pressure Below 2.5 bar CLT Above 102 °C Oil Temp Above 125 °C Fuel Level Below 10% Battery Below 11.5 V The limit for each data item can be changed in DashTune, in General Setting → Data Sources . Tap the banner to silence that warning for 60 seconds. Gauge colors in all themes follow the same limits: normal, yellow when nearing the limit, then red when past it. Fuel consumption (km/l) ¶ The dash calculates fuel consumption in km/l from two pieces of ECU data: Fuel flow , for example from rusEFI or Haltech Vehicle speed (VSS) The figure appears in themes that show it, or you can add it yourself through Customize by choosing KM/L in one of the data panels. When the vehicle is stopped or moving very slowly (below 3 km/h), the figure is 0. If your ECU does not send fuel flow or speed, this value is not available. Extra inputs: turn signal, head light, and fuel level ¶ For ECUs that do not send this data, signals from the car can be connected to spare pins on the Dash R4 and then set up in DashTune in the Extra inputs menu. Important: all pins work at 3.3 V . A 12 V signal must go through optocoupler protection. Do not connect car wires directly to the pins. Pin choices, settings, and fuel level calibration are on the Dash R4 Extra Inputs page. DashTune App Guide ¶ DashTune is an Android app for setting up the dash from your phone over Bluetooth . Getting the app: go to www.mazduino.com and look for the DashTune section on the home page. The app is still in closed testing, so access is granted per account. Enter the email address of your Google Play account there, and an invitation will be sent by email. Connecting for the first time ¶ Turn the ignition key on until the dash lights up. Open DashTune, go to the Device tab, and press Add Dash . Press Scan . The dash appears with the name MazduinoDash-R4 . Choose that dash. Once connected, the app goes straight to the menu page. If it is not found: make sure the phone's Bluetooth is on, the dash is powered on, and the dash is not connected to another phone. A dash that has been connected before is remembered, and the app connects by itself the next time it is opened, also after the dash has been turned off and on again. DashTune menu contents ¶ Menu Function Themes Installed themes, Theme Store, and Customize General Setting ECU type, units, MAP mode, RPM, tank, and warning limits Extra inputs Pins for turn signals, head light (and screen dimming) or theme change button, and fuel level Splash Make your own splash screen Info Firmware version and device status Update Firmware Update the dash firmware Splash screen ¶ The splash screen shows for a few seconds when the dash is turned on, then changes to the theme. In the Splash menu, choose how to make it: Layers : arrange images, logos, and text in layers. Each layer can have its own entrance animation (for example fade, pop, spin, slide, flicker, glitch, drop) and appear one after another. Many fonts and text effects are available, plus a button to remove an image's background. GIF : choose a GIF file from the phone. Video : choose a video from the gallery, then set its length (1–8 seconds), the frames per second, and whether it loops. GIFs and videos are converted on the phone first so the dash can play them smoothly. The longer the animation, the larger the file and the longer the dash takes to start, so the app limits it to about 2 MB and cuts off the end if it is larger. Once sent, press Play on the dash or Restart the dash on the same page to see the result right away. Like themes, the splash is sent over the dash's WiFi, so keep the phone screen on and do not close the app until it finishes. Firmware update ¶ Go to the Update Firmware menu. The app checks the server for the latest version and shows the version installed now. If there is a new version, press the update button. During the update, the dashboard keeps showing until the firmware has been fully sent, then the dash restarts by itself with the new firmware, and DashTune reconnects. If the new firmware fails to start, the dash automatically goes back to the previous firmware. Warning : Do not update while driving. The dash refuses updates while the engine is running. Make sure the vehicle is in a safe state, power is not interrupted, and the app is not closed until it finishes. Relay feature: Google Maps and music ¶ DashTune can forward Google Maps directions and the song that is playing to the dash. The settings are in the More → Relay tab. Directions appear at the top of the screen as a short, slightly transparent notification, then go away by themselves. The notification appears again when there is a new turn or road, or when the distance to the next turn drops below 200 meters. The song title appears briefly when the song changes or when it is played/paused. The song that is playing can also be viewed and controlled from the dash menu, under Music . Tap a notification to close it sooner. This feature needs notification access permission on the phone, and the app takes you to that settings page the first time it is turned on. References ¶ Mazduino Website - https://www.mazduino.com/ Mazduino Wiki - https://wiki.mazduino.com/ Mazduino Github - https://github.com/mazduino/mazduino

docs.text: Some Dash R4 themes: Street (default), Wangan Night, Classic Beetle, Motorsport, Car Status, Retro VFD, Synthwave, Halo, Ink Wave, and Classic Mazduino Dash R4 is a round 4 inch dash display with a touch screen. What it shows comes as themes , which you can install, remove, and adjust yourself from the DashTune app over Bluetooth. The choices range from racing gauges and classic gauges to themes with a photo of your own car. Variant Screen Size Connector Dash R4 4 inch, round DTM4 (Deutsch DTM 4 Pin)
docs.title: Overview

docs.text: Dozens of ready-to-install themes from the Theme Store in DashTune, with up to 10 themes stored on the dash at once. The Street theme is built into the firmware and is always there. You can change what each data panel in a theme shows, for example from Oil Pressure to IAT. Supports rusEFI , Haltech , MaxxECU , ECUMASTER EMU Black , Link Generic Dash , Speeduino , OBD-II , and M-Link ( CAN IO Extender ). Fuel consumption (km/l) is calculated on the dash, if the ECU sends fuel flow and speed data. Warnings (alarms) for Oil Pressure, Fuel Pressure, CLT, Oil Temp, Fuel Level, and Battery. Extra inputs : turn signal, head light, and fuel level signals can be taken from the car, and the screen dims automatically when the lights are on. The head light input can also be used for a theme change button. Google Maps directions and music from your phone show up as short notifications on the screen. Your own splash screen at power-up, which can be animated, or made from a GIF or video. Firmware updates through the app, with no cable.
docs.title: Key Features

docs.text: Dash R4 uses the same DTM4 (Deutsch DTM 4 Pin) connector as Racedash Pro , both in physical form and in the function of each pin. A cable from a Racedash Pro can be used as is. Dash connector side Cable connector side Pin No. Description 1 12V Power Supply 2 Ground 3 CAN High / TX 4 CAN Low / RX Note: Pins 3 and 4 work as CAN High/CAN Low for all ECUs that use CAN Bus (rusEFI, Haltech, MaxxECU, ECUMASTER, Link, OBD-II, M-Link). For Speeduino ECUs only, pins 3 and 4 work as Serial TX/RX , because Speeduino has no native CAN Bus.
docs.title: DTM4 / 4 Pin Connector

docs.text: ECU Connection rusEFI CAN Bus 500 kbps Haltech CAN Bus 1 Mbps MaxxECU CAN Bus 500 kbps ECUMASTER EMU Black CAN Bus 1 Mbps Link Generic Dash CAN Bus 1 Mbps Speeduino Serial OBD-II CAN Bus (ISO 15765-4) M-Link (CAN IO Extender) CAN Bus 500 kbps The ECU type is selected from the menu on the dash screen ( Settings → ECU ) or from DashTune ( General Setting ). No firmware change is needed , and the CAN speed adjusts by itself. Switching between ECUs that both use CAN Bus takes effect immediately, without a restart. Switching from or to Speeduino only takes effect after the dash is turned off and on again, because the function of pins 3 and 4 changes too. What must be enabled on each ECU is covered in ECU Configuration for Racedash . The settings are the same for Dash R4. OBD-II : not every OBD-II car can be read, and the data depends on what your car answers. The limits are the same as on Racedash Pro; read OBD-II limitations before buying for OBD-II use.
docs.title: Supported ECUs

docs.text: A theme is the look of the dashboard. Each theme carries its own gauge layout, colors, and images, like the examples in the Overview . The full list is in the DashTune Theme Store , and new themes keep being added.
docs.title: Themes

docs.text: Swipe left or right on the screen to move to the next theme. Or open the dash menu, choose Themes , then tap the theme you want. The dash remembers the last theme shown. If you want the dash to always start with a particular theme, open Themes in the dash menu and press Set default on that theme.
docs.title: Switching themes

docs.text: Connect DashTune to the dash (see Connecting for the first time ). Open the Themes menu. It shows the themes already installed on the dash, with their images, and how many there are (for example "4 of 10 themes on the dash"). Open the Theme Store , choose a theme, then press download. The theme is sent to the dash over the dash's WiFi. This runs by itself, so keep the phone screen on and do not close the app until it finishes. The dash stores at most 10 themes . When it is full, DashTune asks which theme to remove to make room for the new one. A removed theme stays in the Theme Store and can be installed again at any time. If an installed theme has a newer version in the store, DashTune marks it with UPDATE .
docs.title: Installing themes from DashTune

docs.text: In the Themes menu, choose an installed theme and press Customize . What can be adjusted differs per theme: Data panel contents : the panels are named Data 1 , Data 2 , and so on. Choose the data to show in that panel, for example Oil Pressure, Fuel Pressure, CLT, IAT, AFR, Battery, or KM/L. Car photo (Car Status theme): replace the default car photo with a photo of your own car. Text (for example the Ink Wave and Sticker Bomb themes): replace the text on the theme with the name of your car or team. Colors and other options the theme provides. Changes are sent to the dash and stay saved even when the dash is turned off.
docs.title: Adjusting a theme (Customize)

docs.text: In Customize , choose Change photo , then Take a photo or Choose from gallery . A photo of the car from the front side gives the best result. Choose how to handle the photo background : Automatic : the app cuts the car out of its background by itself. Manual : erase the background with your finger, using the Erase , Restore , and Undo buttons. Keep : the photo is used as it is, background included. Drag and pinch the photo so the car fits inside the frame. The frame shows the area that appears on the dash. Tap the lights you are asked for (for example the headlights), following the Example below the frame. This tells the dash where the lights are that light up with data from the ECU. Press Save to send the photo to the dash.
docs.title: Using a photo of your own car (Car Status)

docs.text: Mazduino LITE v0.3 ¶ Introduction ¶ Mazduino LITE v0.3 is the latest version of the Mazduino LITE ECU family. It is designed for 4-cylinder engines with 4 injector channels and 2 ignition channels. Compared with v0.2, the board is practically the same; what has been added is an I2C header for add-on devices. Firmware : LITE runs rusEFI, and it can also run Speeduino firmware, using the build made for Mazduino Compact rather than a separate build. Both have been tested running. See the Downloads page . Changes in v0.3 from v0.2: I2C Header (J10) : The two pins SDA and SCL are brought out to a header, in line with the existing RX/TX serial header. It is the same bus used by the internal barometric sensor Pinout unchanged The 33-pin main connector and the MCU pin mapping are identical to v0.2 (verified pin by pin from the design files). A v0.2 wiring harness and firmware configuration can be used directly without changes. Carried over from v0.2: IGBT footprint D2Pak to 263 (common & easy to find) Internal barometric sensor (optional) Improved PCB traces Key Features ¶ Input System ¶ Trigger Input : CKP and CMP for Hall/Optical sensors VR Support : Variable Reluctance sensors with a conditioner module (the VR module is optional and not fitted unless chosen at purchase; hall and optical sensors do not need it) Analog Inputs : 6x (0-5V) for MAP, TPS, IAT, CLT, O2, and a spare Digital Inputs : 5x pullup for AC Switch, VSS, Clutch, and launch control Sensor Power : Regulated 5V with internal fuse protection Internal Barometer : Optional, not fitted by default unless requested (since v0.2) Output System ¶ Injection : 4x high-current drivers for sequential or batch mode Ignition : 2x outputs with Smart Coil (5V/12V) and IGBT support Common, easy-to-find D2Pak to 263 IGBT footprint (since v0.2) The internal IGBTs are optional and depend on the variant chosen at purchase: COP only (no IGBTs, for smart coils / Coil On Plug) or IGBT (IGBTs fitted, for dumb coils) Control : 5x relay outputs for fuel pump, fan, AC, main relay, tachometer Idle Control : 2x PWM outputs for the ISC valve Communication ¶ Hardware Configuration ¶ Critical Jumper Settings ¶ IMPORTANT : The jumper configuration must be correct before power-up! Top Side Board ¶ Coil Voltage : 12V/5V selection (default depends on coil type) CAN Terminator : Enable/disable the terminator resistor VR Conditioner : 8-pin connector for the VR module (optional, fitted only when chosen at purchase) Bottom Side Board ¶ Tacho Signal : 5V/12V output selection (default 12V) IGN1/IGN2 Mode : Smart Coil/IGBT selection (JP3/JP4) Internal IGBT with a D2Pak to 263 footprint (common & easy to find) IGBT mode only applies to the IGBT variant; the COP only variant is used with smart coils VR1/Hall, VR2/Hall : Input type selection Digital Pullup : Enable internal pullup resistors CAN Power : 12V/5V on the CAN connector Improvements Carried Over from v0.2 ¶ Main Improvements: PCB Traces : Improved routing and corrected traces for easier jumper setup IGBT Compatibility : A more common, easier-to-find footprint Barometer Support : Mounting for an internal barometric sensor (optional) Pin Assignment : Optimized pin assignment for the 33-pin connector I2C Header (New in v0.3) ¶ The two I2C bus pins are brought out to header J10 , in line with the RX/TX serial header that already existed on v0.2. J10 Pin Signal MCU Pin 1 SDA PB11 2 SCL PB10 Things to watch: 3.3V level : This bus runs at 3.3V; both lines are already pulled up to 3.3V on the board. Do not connect an I2C module whose lines run at 5V without a level shifter, because that voltage goes straight into the MCU pins Pull-ups already fitted : Add-on modules do not need their own pull-ups Only two lines : This header carries only SDA and SCL. There is no power or ground on it, so an add-on module has to take power and ground from somewhere else Shared bus : This is the same bus as the internal barometric sensor. docs.text: Mazduino Mega100 ¶ Overview ¶ The Mazduino Mega100 is an STM32F407 MCU board with the same size and headers as the Arduino Mega 2560. It plugs into the Arduino Mega socket on a Speeduino board in place of the Arduino Mega, so an existing Speeduino board can run the rusEFI Mazduino firmware. With the Mega100, a Speeduino board gets a 168 MHz ARM Cortex-M4 MCU, USB, a microSD slot, CAN bus, and rusEFI firmware features such as Lua, boost, VVT, launch control and data logging. Injector, coil, trigger, sensor and output pins are set from TunerStudio with a single preset button for the Speeduino board in use. This documentation follows the Mega100 v1.3 hardware (Mega converter v1.3). Render of rev1.2. The component layout on v1.3 may differ slightly. Firmware Variants ¶ There are two firmware builds, chosen by the STM32 chip fitted: Firmware Chip Flash Notes mazduino-mega100 STM32F407VGT6 1 MB Full features: Lua, ETB, traction control, software knock, SD card logging, automatic transmission (TCU) mazduino-mega100-512 STM32F407VET6 512 KB Reduced features to fit: no Lua, ETB, traction control, software knock, SD card logging, boost, launch, anti-lag, VVT, speed sensor, alternator, main relay or TCU A full feature comparison per board is in FEATURES.md . Mega100 and Mega100-512 have no BIGFUEL variant. Mazduino recommends the rusEFI Mazduino firmware from the Downloads page. Speeduino firmware is also available for the 1 MB Mega100, but it is still pre-release and not yet tested on hardware . Mega100-512 is not supported by the Speeduino firmware. See Speeduino Firmware . Buffered and Unbuffered Versions ¶ The Mega100 comes in two versions. The difference is the voltage of the digital outputs (D pins) that drive the injectors, coils and other outputs on the Speeduino board: Version Digital output Notes Buffered 5V Outputs raised to 5V like the Arduino Mega Unbuffered 3.3V Outputs directly from the MCU The Arduino Mega outputs 5V, and some Speeduino boards use MOSFETs that need a 5V gate to turn fully on. For the unbuffered version, replace those MOSFETs with logic-level types that turn fully on at a 3.3V gate. MOSFET not fully on A 5V-gate MOSFET driven with only 3.3V does not turn fully on, so the MOSFET can get hot and the output may not work correctly. Check the datasheet of the MOSFETs on your Speeduino board before using the unbuffered version. The word "buffer" here refers to the digital outputs. The A0–A15 analog inputs have their own buffer (see Hardware Features). The v1.3 schematic used for this page is the unbuffered version. Hardware Features ¶ STM32F407 MCU (ARM Cortex-M4, 168 MHz), 8 MHz crystal and 32.768 kHz RTC crystal Same size and headers as the Arduino Mega 2560, fits straight into the Speeduino board socket 16 analog inputs (A0–A15) with buffers and voltage dividers, so 0–5V sensor signals are safe for the 3.3V MCU USB Type-B for TunerStudio and firmware updates (DFU), with ESD protection and a polyfuse microSD slot for data logging (SPI3) CAN bus with an on-board transceiver RESET and BOOT buttons to enter DFU mode SWD header for ST-Link Power LED and status LED On-board 3.3V regulator, fed from the Speeduino board's 5V supply Connectors and Headers ¶ Arduino Mega Header ¶ The labels on the back of the board show each header pin name and its STM32 pin. All Arduino Mega headers (D0–D53, A0–A15, power) are in the same positions as on the Arduino Mega 2560. Some pins differ: D21 and D46 are not connected to the MCU. D43 also drives the board status LED (PB7). The presets do not use this pin. A0–A15 are inputs only. Because they go through a buffer, the analog pins cannot be used as outputs. On the 10-pin header next to D8–D13, the SDA and SCL positions carry CANH and CANL , and the AREF position is not connected. Make sure the Speeduino board does not connect anything to the SDA/SCL pins on that header. CAN Bus ¶ CANH and CANL are available on the 2-pin header J11 (pin 1 CANL, pin 2 CANH), and also on the SDA/SCL positions of the 10-pin header described above. The transceiver is already on the board, so CAN wires from a dash, wideband or other device connect directly to CANH/CANL. CAN settings are in CAN Bus Configuration . SWD (J10) ¶ Pin Function 1 3.3V 2 SWDIO 3 SWCLK 4 GND Buttons and LEDs ¶ Component Function RESET Restarts the MCU BOOT Hold during reset or while plugging in USB to enter DFU mode Power LED On when 5V supply is present Status LED Error indicator on PB7 (D43) Installing on a Speeduino Board ¶ Turn off the Speeduino board, then remove the Arduino Mega from its socket. Fit the Mega100 in the same socket, facing the same way as the Arduino Mega. Make sure every pin goes in and none are offset. Flash the mazduino-mega100 firmware (or mazduino-mega100-512 for the 512 KB chip) over USB DFU or ST-Link. See the Flashing section on the Downloads page. Open TunerStudio with the .ini file from the same firmware bundle. Apply the pin preset for your Speeduino board (see the next section). Speeduino Board Pin Presets ¶ Injector, coil, trigger, sensor and output pins differ between Speeduino boards. The firmware provides presets that fill them all in at once. In TunerStudio, open Controller → Base Tunes , then press the Speeduino pins button that matches your board. Presets are available for Speeduino v0.2, v0.3, v0.4, 96-97 MX5 PNP, NA6 MX5 PNP, UA4C, and several other Speeduino boards. The full list is shown in that menu. When the button is pressed, the ECU saves the new pins immediately. Reconnect TunerStudio so it reads the new values, then turn the ECU off and on again. A preset fills in: Injectors 1–4 and coils 1–4 Trigger (crank) and cam inputs, or the second trigger for boards that use one TPS, MAP, IAT, CLT, O2, battery voltage and baro Fuel pump, tach, fan, idle, boost and VVT Idle stepper driver, VSS, flex fuel and launch, if the board has them A preset clears the old pins on the Mega header before filling in the new ones, so no pins are left over from another board. Pins that the Speeduino board does not have are left empty. After a preset is applied, pins can still be changed manually in TunerStudio. New firmware uses the Speeduino v0.4 preset as the default. 01-05 MX5 PNP board There is no preset for the 01-05 MX5 PNP, because coil 2 on that board is on D43 (status LED) and injector 2 is on D46 (not connected). Pin Mapping Examples ¶ Two examples of preset results. The header pin is the pin number on the Arduino Mega header, and the STM32 pin is the name shown in TunerStudio. Speeduino v0.4 ¶ Function Header pin STM32 pin Injector 1 D8 PD8 Injector 2 D9 PD9 Injector 3 D10 PD10 Injector 4 D11 PD11 Coil 1 D40 PE2 Coil 2 D38 PE3 Coil 3 D52 PC13 Coil 4 D50 PE7 Trigger (crank) D19 PD3 Cam D18 PD4 TPS A2 PA2 MAP A3 PA3 IAT A0 PA0 CLT A1 PA1 O2 1 A8 PB0 Battery voltage A4 PA4 Baro A5 PA5 Fuel pump D45 PE11 Tach D49 PE8 Fan D47 PE9 Idle 1 D5 PB13 Idle 2 D6 PB14 Boost D7 PB15 VVT 1 D4 PB12 Stepper direction D16 PB10 Stepper step D17 PB11 Stepper enable D24 PA15 Flex fuel D2 PD7 Launch D51 PB8 O2 2 and VSS are not filled in by this preset. D16/D17 are used by the stepper driver, so the Bluetooth port is off. Pin A3 is used for MAP, so software knock cannot be used. UA4C ¶ Function Header pin STM32 pin Injector 1 D8 PD8 Injector 2 D7 PB15 Injector 3 D6 PB14 Injector 4 D5 PB13 Coil 1 D35 PE15 Coil 2 D36 PE4 Coil 3 D33 PD13 Coil 4 D34 PE5 Trigger (crank) D19 PD3 Cam D18 PD4 TPS A3 PA3 MAP A0 PA0 IAT A5 PA5 CLT A4 PA4 O2 1 A1 PA1 O2 2 A9 PB1 Battery voltage A2 PA2 Baro A7 PA7 Fuel pump D23 PC8 Tach D22 PC9 Fan D24 PA15 Idle 1 D9 PD9 Idle 2 D10 PD10 Boost D12 PA8 VVT 1 D11 PD11 Stepper direction D32 PD12 Stepper step D31 PD15 Stepper enable D30 PD14 VSS D2 PD7 Launch D37 PE14 Flex fuel is not filled in by this preset. D16/D17 are not used, so the Bluetooth port stays available. Pin A3 is used for TPS, so software knock cannot be used. Feature Notes ¶ Bluetooth ¶ The TunerStudio Bluetooth port is on D16 (TX, PB10) and D17 (RX, PB11). Many Speeduino boards use D16/D17 for the idle stepper driver, including Speeduino v0.4. With such a preset, the Bluetooth port is turned off automatically. Wiring details are in Bluetooth . Software Knock ¶ Software knock reads pin PA3 , which is A3 on the Mega header. On presets that use A3 for a sensor, for example MAP on Speeduino v0.4 or TPS on UA4C, leave knock turned off. SD Card ¶ The mazduino-mega100 firmware uses the on-board microSD slot for data logging. The mazduino-mega100-512 firmware has no SD card logging. Header to STM32 Pin Table ¶ TunerStudio shows pins by their STM32 pin name. Use this table when changing pins manually. docs.text: Mazduino Mini 6CH (v1.0 - v1.2) ¶ Overview ¶ Mazduino Mini 6CH v1.0-v1.2 is a compact 6-channel Engine Control Unit designed for use with rusEFI and Speeduino firmware. Built around a powerful 32-bit ARM Cortex-M4 processor, it provides comprehensive engine management in a compact form factor suited to 6-cylinder engines, or 4-cylinder engines with additional high-current outputs. Key Features ¶ Primary trigger input for VR, hall or optical CKP sensors Secondary trigger input for VR, hall or optical CMP sensors 7 analog inputs (0-5V) for MAP, TPS, IAT, CLT, O2, and 2 spares that can be used for a fuel pressure sensor or other sensors 5V sensor power supply with internal fuse protection 4 pullup digital inputs for AC Switch, VSS, Clutch, Launch Control 8x 3A high-current low-side drivers for high-impedance injectors, idle PWM (ISC), Boost, VVT and more 5x low-current low-side drivers for main relay, fuel pump, AC compressor, fan, and tachometer control 6x 12V or 5V outputs for ignition coil signals Support for an add-on VR Conditioner Module Support for an add-on Idle Stepper Module 168 MHz ARM Cortex-M4 processor Data communication via CANbus Data communication via USB Type-C Serial RX/TX communication 48-pin automotive connector SD card for data logging Wiring and Installation ¶ Connector Pin Mapping ¶ Mazduino Mini 6CH uses a 48-pin Yamaha ECU connector docs.text: Mazduino Mini 6CH (v1.3) ¶ Overview ¶ Mazduino Mini 6CH v1.3 is a compact 6-channel Engine Control Unit designed for use with rusEFI and Speeduino firmware. Built around a powerful 32-bit ARM Cortex-M4 processor, it provides comprehensive engine management in a compact form factor suited to 6-cylinder engines, or 4-cylinder engines with additional high-current outputs. New Features in v1.3: Knock Input : Knock sensor support for engine knock detection ETB (Electronic Throttle Body) : Integrated electronic throttle control Key Features ¶ Primary trigger input for VR, hall or optical CKP sensors Secondary trigger input for VR, hall or optical CMP sensors 7 analog inputs (0-5V) for MAP, TPS, IAT, CLT, O2, and 2 spares that can be used for a fuel pressure sensor or other sensors 5V sensor power supply with internal fuse protection 4 pullup digital inputs for AC Switch, VSS, Clutch, Launch Control 8x 3A high-current low-side drivers for high-impedance injectors, idle PWM (ISC), Boost, VVT and more 5x low-current low-side drivers for main relay, fuel pump, AC compressor, fan, and tachometer control 6x 12V or 5V outputs for ignition coil signals Knock Input (v1.3) : Knock sensor input for engine knock detection ETB Support (v1.3) : Electronic Throttle Body control with TPS1 and TPS2 Support for an add-on VR Conditioner Module Support for an add-on Idle Stepper Module 168 MHz ARM Cortex-M4 processor Data communication via CANbus Data communication via USB Type-C Serial RX/TX communication 48-pin automotive connector SD card for data logging Jumper Configuration ¶ Mazduino Mini 6CH v1.3 has a solder jumper system that lets you customize functions to suit your application. These jumpers give configuration flexibility without changing the firmware, for good compatibility with a wide range of engine setups. Top Configuration Zone (Right) ¶ JP11 - Tachometer Pullup ¶ Function : Sets the voltage of the tachometer output signal Options : 12V or 5V Application : Match it to what your vehicle's dashboard accepts Ignition VDrive Jumper ¶ Function : Sets the ignition signal voltage for Smart Coil Only Options : 12V or 5V signal Smart Coil Only : This jumper is only for smart coils with a built-in driver IMPORTANT : Dump coils need an external IGBT Knock/PC13 Input Selection ¶ Knock Mode : Knock sensor input for engine knock detection (default) PC13 Mode : Direct access to the MCU pin for custom functions New in v1.3 : Integrated knock detection support Middle Configuration Zone ¶ JP5 & JP4 - Sensor Pullup Configuration ¶ JP5 : 5V pullup for the CKP (Crankshaft Position) signal JP4 : 5V pullup for the CMP (Camshaft Position) signal Benefit : Clean, stable trigger signals JP2 & JP3 - Sensor Type Selection ¶ JP2 : CKP signal mode (VR or Hall sensor) JP3 : CMP signal mode (VR or Hall sensor) Flexibility : Compatible with many types of position sensors Left Configuration Zone ¶ JP10 - CAN Bus Controller ¶ Function : Enables the TJA1051T/3 CAN bus IC Application : High-speed data communication with other devices Protocol : Supports the automotive CAN 2.0 standard JP6 - Stepper Motor Enable ¶ Function : Controls activation of the stepper motor driver Note : Consult the schematic for the best configuration Application : High-precision Idle Air Control (IAC) JP7 & JP8 - Knock Sensor Filter Bypass ¶ Function : Filter bypass for the knock sensor JP7 : Knock channel 1 filter bypass JP8 : Knock channel 2 filter bypass Advanced Feature : Fine-tuning of knock detection sensitivity Jumper Configuration Tips ¶ Optimal Settings: ¶ Smart Coils : Use VDrive 5V for coils with a 5V signal and 12V for coils with a 12V signal Dump/Conventional Coils : Require an external IGBT VR Sensors : Select VR mode (signal goes through the VR Conditioner module) and remove the pullup — the pullup loads the VR sensor coil Hall / Optical Sensors : Select Hall mode and fit the pullup (JP5 for CKP, JP4 for CMP). Hall sensors are usually open-collector and cannot produce a HIGH level on their own; without a pullup the trigger pin floats and picks up noise, which causes trigger errors while the engine runs. Only remove the pullup for sensors with a push-pull 5V output Best Practices: ¶ Pre-Installation : Configure the jumpers before final installation Documentation : Write down the jumper configuration docs.text: Mazduino Mini 6CH (v1.3B) ¶ Overview ¶ Mazduino Mini 6CH v1.3B is a revised and improved version of v1.3, designed as a better-optimized 6-channel Engine Control Unit. docs.text: Mazduino Mini 6CH v1.3B is a revised and improved version of v1.3, designed as a better-optimized 6-channel Engine Control Unit. docs.text: Mazduino Mini 6CH (v1.3C) ¶ Overview ¶ Mazduino Mini 6CH v1.3C is the latest production version of the Mini 6CH line, a refined and improved version of v1.3B as a more capable 6-channel Engine Control Unit. Built around a powerful 32-bit ARM Cortex-M4 180 MHz processor, it provides comprehensive engine management in a compact form factor suited to 6-cylinder engines, or 4-cylinder engines with additional high-current outputs. v1.3C improvements over v1.3B: MCU Pin Optimization : TPS moved to PA6 and Battery/Voltage Reference moved to PA7 for better signal routing Single Knock Input : Consolidated from 2 knock inputs (PC0, PC1) to 1 more efficient knock input (PA3) Separate Ignition VDrive : Two separate VDrive jumpers, one for ignition channels 1-4 and one for ignition channels 5-6, for more flexible voltage configuration Channel Flexibility : 6 ignition channels and 6 injection channels, all configurable to suit the application Key Features ¶ Primary trigger input for VR, hall or optical CKP sensors Secondary trigger input for VR, hall or optical CMP sensors 8 analog inputs (0-5V) for MAP, TPS, IAT, CLT, O2, and 3 spares, including a dedicated analog input for TPS2/ETB that can be used for a fuel pressure sensor or other sensors 5V sensor power supply with internal fuse protection 4 pullup digital inputs for AC Switch, VSS, Clutch, Launch Control 8x 3A high-current low-side drivers for high-impedance injectors, idle PWM (ISC), Boost, VVT and more 5x low-current low-side drivers for main relay, fuel pump, AC compressor, fan, and tachometer control 6x ignition outputs with separate VDrive for channels 1-4 and channels 5-6 (each configurable for 5V or 12V) Knock Input (v1.3C) : One optimized knock sensor input (PA3) ETB Support : Electronic Throttle Body control with TPS1 and TPS2 Support for an add-on VR Conditioner Module Support for an add-on Idle Stepper Module 180 MHz ARM Cortex-M4 processor Data communication via CANbus Data communication via USB Type-C Jumper Configuration ¶ Mazduino Mini 6CH v1.3C has a system of solder jumpers that lets you customize functions to suit your application. The jumpers give you configuration flexibility without changing the firmware, so the board works with a wide range of engine setups. Top Configuration Zone (Right) ¶ JP11 - Tachometer Pullup ¶ Function : Sets the voltage of the tachometer output signal Options : 12V or 5V Application : Match it to what your vehicle's dashboard accepts Ignition VDrive 1-4 Jumper ¶ Function : Sets the ignition signal voltage for channels Ignition 1, 2, 3, 4 — Smart Coil Only Options : 12V or 5V signal Smart Coil Only : This jumper is only for smart coils with a built-in driver Alternative : When channels 1-4 are used for 4-cylinder ignition, channels 5-6 stay independent IMPORTANT : Dump coils require an external IGBT Ignition VDrive 5-6 Jumper (New in v1.3C) ¶ Function : Sets the signal voltage for channels Ignition 5 and 6 separately from channels 1-4 Options : 12V or 5V signal Flexibility : Channels 5-6 can be set to a different voltage than channels 1-4 Alternative Use : When used as switching control, match the voltage (5V or 12V) to the load Location : Bottom of the PCB (see jumper photo) IMPORTANT : Dump coils require an external IGBT Knock/PC13 Input Selection ¶ Knock Mode : Knock sensor input for engine knock detection (default) PC13 Mode : Direct access to the MCU pin for custom functions v1.3C : One optimized knock input on MCU pin PA3 Middle Configuration Zone ¶ JP5 & JP4 - Stepper Motor Enable ¶ Function : Controls enabling of the stepper motor driver Note : Consult the schematic for the optimal configuration Application : High-precision Idle Air Control (IAC) JP7 & JP8 - for alternative use on 4-cylinder engines Reference : More sensor wiring information on the Speeduino Wiki Hardware Information ¶ Mazduino Mini 6CH v1.3C is designed around an ARM Cortex-M4 180 MHz as the main MCU, delivering high performance at a 180MHz clock. It supports several add-on modules such as the VR Conditioner Module and the Idle Stepper Module. By default, Mazduino Mini 6CH v1.3C only supports digital CKP and CMP signals, such as hall and optical sensors. Vehicles that still use VR sensors need the VR Module added (or the sensor can be converted to hall). For idle, Mazduino Mini 6CH v1.3C supports Idle PWM, with 2 low-side MOSFET outputs that can be used for IDLE PWM control. Idle Control with a stepper motor requires an add-on module, the Idle Stepper Motor Module. A DRV8825 driver can be used here. There are solder jumpers on the back of the PCB: v1.3C Solder Jumpers: Tach Pullup: Pullup for the tachometer/RPM Speedometer, using 12V or 5V Ignition VDrive 1-4: Signal voltage for Ignition channels 1, 2, 3, 4 (12V or 5V) Ignition VDrive 5-6: Signal voltage for Ignition channels 5 and 6 (12V or 5V) — separate from the 1-4 jumper Knock/MCU PC13: Selects the Knock sensor input or a direct connection to MCU pin PC13 (default is Knock) JP5: CKP/Primary trigger pullup JP4: CMP/Secondary trigger pullup JP2: VR or Hall option for CKP/Primary JP3: VR or Hall option for CMP/Secondary JP6: Idle Stepper bypass JP7 & JP8: Knock filter bypass Pullup Launch: Pullup on the spare input 3 pin when it is used for a launch control activation button or another input that needs a pullup Software Tuning ¶ Download Software ¶ Download TunerStudio: TunerStudio Downloads v1.3C-Specific Configuration ¶ TPS Pin : Make sure the TPS configuration uses PA6 (not PA3 as on v1.3B) Battery/VRef Pin : Make sure the Battery/Voltage Reference configuration uses PA7 Knock Detection : Use PA3 for the single knock sensor configuration ETB Setup : Configure TPS2 on pin 40 AC Switch Logic : Make sure the AC switch configuration uses GROUND logic for ON Pin Mapping : Use the v1.3C-specific pin mapping configuration file Firmware Support ¶ rusEFI : Full support for v1.3C with the updated pin mapping Speeduino : Not supported on v1.3C — use rusEFI Configuration Files : Available on the downloads page Wiring Diagram ¶ Sensor Wiring ¶ Note: Make sure the AC Switch only uses a GROUND signal for the ON state Injector Wiring ¶ Ignition Wiring ¶ v1.3C Important Notes ¶ Ignition System Requirements ¶ Smart Coils : Direct connection supported — VDrive 1-4 and VDrive 5-6 can be set to different voltages (5V or 12V per group) Dump Coils : External IGBT required; the VDrive jumpers are not used for dump coils Migrating from v1.3B ¶ TPS : Update to PA6 (from PA3) — must be changed in the firmware configuration Battery/VRef : Update to PA7 (from PA6) — follows the TPS change Knock : Only one input ( PA3 ) — remove the second knock configuration if present VDrive : Reconfigure the VDrive 1-4 and VDrive 5-6 jumpers separately on the bottom of the PCB Download firmware and configuration files Wiring Harness ¶ Per-pin wire size recommendations for Mazduino Mini 6CH v1.3C, with a count of wires for each size, are in Harness Wire Size Recommendations .

docs.text: Mazduino Mini 6CH v1.3C is the latest production version of the Mini 6CH line, a refined and improved version of v1.3B as a more capable 6-channel Engine Control Unit. Built around a powerful 32-bit ARM Cortex-M4 180 MHz processor, it provides comprehensive engine management in a compact form factor suited to 6-cylinder engines, or 4-cylinder engines with additional high-current outputs. v1.3C improvements over v1.3B: MCU Pin Optimization : TPS moved to PA6 and Battery/Voltage Reference moved to PA7 for better signal routing Single Knock Input : Consolidated from 2 knock inputs (PC0, PC1) to 1 more efficient knock input (PA3) Separate Ignition VDrive : Two separate VDrive jumpers, one for ignition channels 1-4 and one for ignition channels 5-6, for more flexible voltage configuration Channel Flexibility : 6 ignition channels and 6 injection channels, all configurable to suit the application
docs.title: Overview

docs.text: Primary trigger input for VR, hall or optical CKP sensors Secondary trigger input for VR, hall or optical CMP sensors 8 analog inputs (0-5V) for MAP, TPS, IAT, CLT, O2, and 3 spares, including a dedicated analog input for TPS2/ETB that can be used for a fuel pressure sensor or other sensors 5V sensor power supply with internal fuse protection 4 pullup digital inputs for AC Switch, VSS, Clutch, Launch Control 8x 3A high-current low-side drivers for high-impedance injectors, idle PWM (ISC), Boost, VVT and more 5x low-current low-side drivers for main relay, fuel pump, AC compressor, fan, and tachometer control 6x ignition outputs with separate VDrive for channels 1-4 and channels 5-6 (each configurable for 5V or 12V) Knock Input (v1.3C) : One optimized knock sensor input (PA3) ETB Support : Electronic Throttle Body control with TPS1 and TPS2 Support for an add-on VR Conditioner Module Support for an add-on Idle Stepper Module 180 MHz ARM Cortex-M4 processor Data communication via CANbus Data communication via USB Type-C Serial RX/TX communication 48-pin automotive connector SD card for data logging

docs.text: Mazduino Mini 6CH v1.3C is designed around an ARM Cortex-M4 180 MHz as the main MCU, delivering high performance at a 180MHz clock. It supports several add-on modules such as the VR Conditioner Module and the Idle Stepper Module. By default, Mazduino Mini 6CH v1.3C only supports digital CKP and CMP signals, such as hall and optical sensors. Vehicles that still use VR sensors need the VR Module added (or the sensor can be converted to hall). For idle, Mazduino Mini 6CH v1.3C supports Idle PWM, with 2 low-side MOSFET outputs that can be used for IDLE PWM control. Idle Control with a stepper motor requires an add-on module, the Idle Stepper Motor Module. A DRV8825 driver can be used here. There are solder jumpers on the back of the PCB: v1.3C Solder Jumpers: Tach Pullup: Pullup for the tachometer/RPM Speedometer, using 12V or 5V Ignition VDrive 1-4: Signal voltage for Ignition channels 1, 2, 3, 4 (12V or 5V) Ignition VDrive 5-6: Signal voltage for Ignition channels 5 and 6 (12V or 5V) — separate from the 1-4 jumper Knock/MCU PC13: Selects the Knock sensor input or a direct connection to MCU pin PC13 (default is Knock) JP5: CKP/Primary trigger pullup JP4: CMP/Secondary trigger pullup JP2: VR or Hall option for CKP/Primary JP3: VR or Hall option for CMP/Secondary JP6: Idle Stepper bypass JP7 & JP8: Knock filter bypass Pullup Launch: Pullup on the spare input 3 pin when it is used for a launch control activation button or another input that needs a pullup

docs.text: Mazduino Mini 6CH (v1.3D) ¶ Overview ¶ Mazduino Mini 6CH v1.3D is the latest production version of the Mini 6CH line. Functionally this board is exactly the same as v1.3C — what changed is the circuitry around the analog and CAN sections. Built around a powerful 32-bit ARM Cortex-M4 180 MHz processor, it provides comprehensive engine management in a compact form factor suited to 6-cylinder engines, or 4-cylinder engines with additional high-current outputs. v1.3D changes from v1.3C: More Stable Analog Sensor Readings : The reference voltage for analog readings now has its own source, instead of being derived from the 5V rail as on v1.3C. The analog section is also supplied through a path separate from the digital section Onboard CAN Termination : A fixed 120 Ω resistor between CANH and CANL (pins 4 and 21). See the important note on termination before connecting to a bus that already has terminators JP9 Without Factory Bridge : The Knock/PC13 jumper uses an open solder jumper footprint — on v1.3C the Knock side was bridged at the factory; on v1.3D you decide Pinout unchanged The 48-pin connector pinout and the MCU pin mapping are identical to v1.3C (verified pin by pin from the design files). v1.3C tunes and firmware configuration can be used directly without changes. Improvements inherited from v1.3C (relative to v1.3B): MCU Pin Optimization : TPS moved to PA6 and Battery/Voltage Reference moved to PA7 for better signal routing Single Knock Input : Consolidated from 2 knock inputs (PC0, PC1) to 1 more efficient knock input (PA3) Separate Ignition VDrive : Two separate VDrive jumpers, one for ignition channels 1-4 and one for ignition channels 5-6, for more flexible voltage configuration Channel Flexibility : 6 ignition channels and 6 injection channels, all configurable to suit the application Key Features ¶ Primary trigger input for VR, hall or optical CKP sensors Secondary trigger input for VR, hall or optical CMP sensors 8 analog inputs (0-5V) for MAP, TPS, IAT, CLT, O2, and 3 spares, including a dedicated analog input for TPS2/ETB that can be used for a fuel pressure sensor or other sensors 5V sensor power supply with internal fuse protection 4 pullup digital inputs for AC Switch, VSS, Clutch, Launch Control 8x 3A high-current low-side drivers for high-impedance injectors, idle PWM (ISC), Boost, VVT and more 5x low-current low-side drivers for main relay, fuel pump, AC compressor, fan, and tachometer control 6x ignition outputs with separate VDrive for channels 1-4 and channels 5-6 (each configurable for 5V or 12V) Knock Input : One optimized knock sensor input (PA3) ETB Support : Electronic Throttle Body control with TPS1 and TPS2 Support for an add-on VR Conditioner Module Support for an add-on Idle Stepper Module 180 MHz ARM Cortex-M4 processor Data communication via CANbus Data communication via USB Type-C Serial RX/TX communication 48-pin automotive connector SD card for data logging 6CH Channel Configuration ¶ Mazduino Mini 6CH v1.3D has 6 ignition channels and 6 injection channels, all configurable to suit the application. Ignition Channel (6x) ¶ Channel Default Use Alternative Use Ignition 1-4 Ignition channels for cylinders 1-4 — Ignition 5-6 Ignition channels for cylinders 5-6 5V or 12V switching control (on/off or PWM) On 4-cylinder engines, ignition channels 5 and 6 can be used as switching control outputs (5V or 12V), depending on the VDrive 5-6 jumper setting on the bottom of the PCB. Injection Channel (6x) ¶ Channel Default Use Alternative Use Injector 1-4 Injector channels for cylinders 1-4 — Injector 5-6 Injector channels for cylinders 5-6 Spare high-current low-side output On 4-cylinder engines, injector channels 5 and 6 can be used as low-side outputs for on/off solenoids, boost control, VVT, water/methanol injection, or other PWM control. Jumper Configuration ¶ Mazduino Mini 6CH v1.3D has a system of solder jumpers that lets you customize functions to suit your application. The jumpers give you configuration flexibility without changing the firmware, so the board works with a wide range of engine setups. Top Configuration Zone (Right) ¶ JP11 - Tachometer Pullup ¶ Function : Sets the voltage of the tachometer output signal Options : 12V or 5V Application : Match it to what your vehicle's dashboard accepts Ignition VDrive 1-4 Jumper ¶ Function : Sets the ignition signal voltage for channels Ignition 1, 2, 3, 4 — Smart Coil Only Options : 12V or 5V signal Smart Coil Only : This jumper is only for smart coils with a built-in driver Alternative : When channels 1-4 are used for 4-cylinder ignition, channels 5-6 stay independent IMPORTANT : Dump coils require an external IGBT Ignition VDrive 5-6 Jumper (since v1.3C) ¶ Function : Sets the signal voltage for channels Ignition 5 and 6 separately from channels 1-4 Options : 12V or 5V signal Flexibility : Channels 5-6 can be set to a different voltage than channels 1-4 Alternative Use : When used as switching control, match the voltage (5V or 12V) to the load Location : Bottom of the PCB (see jumper photo) IMPORTANT : Dump coils require an external IGBT Knock/PC13 Input Selection ¶ Knock Mode : Knock sensor input for engine knock detection PC13 Mode : Direct access to the MCU pin for custom functions MCU Pin : One optimized knock input on PA3 Changed in v1.3D : JP9 uses an open solder jumper footprint. On v1.3C the Knock side was connected at the factory; on v1.3D pin 8 is not connected to anything until you bridge one side of JP9. If the knock sensor reads nothing at all on a new board, check JP9 first. Middle Configuration Zone ¶ JP5 & JP4 - Sensor Pullup Configuration ¶ JP5 : 5V pullup for the CKP (Crankshaft Position) signal JP4 : 5V pullup for the CMP (Camshaft Position) signal Benefit : Clean, stable trigger signals JP2 & JP3 - Sensor Type Selection ¶ JP2 : CKP signal mode (VR or Hall sensor) JP3 : CMP signal mode (VR or Hall sensor) Flexibility : Works with many types of position sensors Left Configuration Zone ¶ JP6 - Stepper Motor Enable ¶ Function : Controls enabling of the stepper motor driver Note : Consult the schematic for the optimal configuration Application : High-precision Idle Air Control (IAC) JP7 & JP8 - Knock Sensor Filter Bypass ¶ Function : Bypasses the internal filter for the knock sensor JP7 : Bypasses internal knock filter stage 1 JP8 : Bypasses internal knock filter stage 2 Note : For the single knock input on the ECU connector (pin 8) Jumper Configuration Tips ¶ Optimal Settings: ¶ Smart Coils 1-4 : Set VDrive 1-4 to match the coil specification (5V or 12V) Smart Coils 5-6 : Set VDrive 5-6 to match the coil specification or the alternative load — it can differ from 1-4 Dump/Conventional Coils : Require an external IGBT VR Sensors : Select VR mode (signal goes through the VR Conditioner module) and remove the pullup — a pullup loads the VR sensor coil Hall / Optical Sensors : Select Hall mode and fit the pullup (JP5 for CKP, JP4 for CMP). Hall sensors are usually open-collector and cannot drive a HIGH level on their own; without a pullup the trigger pin floats and picks up noise, which causes trigger errors while the engine is running. Remove the pullup only for sensors with a 5V push-pull output Best Practices: ¶ Pre-Installation : Configure the jumpers before final installation Separate VDrive : Use the independent VDrive 5-6 for mixed-voltage applications Documentation : Write down your jumper configuration for future reference Testing : Verify the signals after changing any jumper Compatibility : Make sure the jumpers match the hardware you are using Special Attention: ¶ Coil Type Is Critical : VDrive is only for smart coils - dump coils need an external IGBT Separate VDrive : VDrive 1-4 and VDrive 5-6 are different jumpers on the bottom of the PCB Solder Carefully : Use the correct soldering temperature Verify Connections : Make sure the solder joints are solid Consult the Schematic : Refer to the diagrams for advanced configuration Power Off : Always switch off power when changing jumpers Wiring and Installation ¶ Connector Pin Mapping ¶ Mazduino Mini 6CH v1.3D uses a 48-pin Yamaha ECU connector with the (PA8), Direction (PB8), Disable (PB9) Separate Ignition VDrive (since v1.3C) ¶ VDrive 1-4 : Solder jumper for the signal voltage of ignition channels 1, 2, 3, 4 (5V or 12V) VDrive 5-6 : Separate solder jumper for the signal voltage of ignition channels 5 and 6 (5V or 12V) Location : Both are on the bottom of the PCB Flexibility : Lets channels 5-6 be set to a different voltage than channels 1-4, as the application requires More Stable Analog Sensor Readings (New in v1.3D) ¶ What changed : The reference voltage for all analog readings now has its own source. On v1.3C that reference was derived from the 5V rail, so it moved with sensor load, battery voltage, and temperature Separate Supply : The analog section is supplied through its own path, filtered from the digital section, so noise from the digital side does not get into the readings Effect : MAP, TPS, IAT, CLT, O2, Battery, and the spare analog inputs are more stable and consistent — most noticeable on the readings used for fueling decisions No Setup Needed : Everything is on the board; there is no jumper or firmware setting that goes with it Calibration Note : Analog sensor calibrations carried over from a v1.3C board should be rechecked — not necessarily changed, but small offsets that were "compensated" in the calibration tables may no longer be needed Onboard CAN Termination (New in v1.3D) ¶ R13 (120 Ω) : Permanently fitted between CANH (pin 4) and CANL (pin 21). There is no jumper to disconnect it When this is correct : The ECU is at an end of the CAN bus. A healthy CAN bus has exactly two 120 Ω terminators, one at each end CAUTION : If the ECU is installed in the middle of a bus whose two ends are already terminated, the total resistance drops to 40 Ω and the bus may fail to communicate. In that case remove one of the other terminators , or lift R13 off the board Other Mazduino devices : Racedash and the WBO CAN Controller may also carry their own terminators — count the terminators across the whole network, not per device VR Conditioner Support ¶ VR1- & VR2- : Input pins for the VR conditioner module (DIP 8) - negative VR1+ & VR2+ : Positive VR sensor inputs Stepper Motor Control ¶ Stepper A1/A2 : Phase A outputs for the stepper motor (DRV8825) Stepper B1/B2 : Phase B outputs for the stepper motor Direction/Enable/Step : Control signals for the stepper driver Installation Guide ¶ Mounting : Mount the ECU in a suitable location with adequate cooling Power Connection : Connect 12V power (pin 1) and ground (pin 22) Sensor Ground : Use the multiple sensor ground pins (37, 38) for clean signals Engine Position Sensors : Connect the CKP/CMP sensors, or use the VR inputs as needed Knock Sensor : First bridge JP9 to the Knock side (v1.3D ships open), then connect the knock sensor to pin 8 ETB Setup : Connect the ETB to pins 33/34 and TPS2 to pin 40 if using an electronic throttle AC Switch : Make sure the AC switch only provides a GROUND signal for the ON state VDrive Configuration : Set the VDrive 1-4 and VDrive 5-6 jumpers separately on the bottom of the PCB to match the coil type or load Spare Channels : Configure injector channels 5-6 and/or ignition channels 5-6 as the application requires Module Installation : Fit the VR-Conditioner and/or Stepper modules if needed Verification : Test all connections before the first startup v1.3D Wiring Notes ¶ CAN Termination : R13 (120 Ω) is permanently fitted on the board. Make sure the whole CAN bus still has exactly two terminators — see Onboard CAN Termination JP9 Open : Pin 8 is connected to neither the Knock circuit nor PC13 until JP9 is bridged Separate VDrive : The VDrive 1-4 and VDrive 5-6 jumpers are on the bottom of the PCB — configure them before final installation AC Switch Logic : Pin 20 accepts GROUND only as the ON signal — do not connect 12V directly TPS MCU Pin : TPS uses PA6 (not PA3 as on v1.3B) — make sure the firmware configuration is correct Spare Channels : Pins 15-16 (Injector 5-6) and Pins 24-25 (Ignition 5-6) are available for alternative use on 4-cylinder engines Reference : More sensor wiring information on the Speeduino Wiki Hardware Information ¶ Mazduino Mini 6CH v1.3D is designed around an ARM Cortex-M4 180 MHz as the main MCU, delivering high performance at a 180MHz clock. docs.text: Smart Coils 1-4 : Set VDrive 1-4 to match the coil specification (5V or 12V) Smart Coils 5-6 : Set VDrive 5-6 to match the coil specification or the alternative load — it can differ from 1-4 Dump/Conventional Coils : Require an external IGBT VR Sensors : Select VR mode (signal goes through the VR Conditioner module) and remove the pullup — a pullup loads the VR sensor coil Hall / Optical Sensors : Select Hall mode and fit the pullup (JP5 for CKP, JP4 for CMP). Hall sensors are usually open-collector and cannot drive a HIGH level on their own; without a pullup the trigger pin floats and picks up noise, which causes trigger errors while the engine is running. Remove the pullup only for sensors with a 5V push-pull output
