docs.text: What changed : The reference voltage for all analog readings now has its own source. On v1.3C that reference was derived from the 5V rail, so it moved with sensor load, battery voltage, and temperature Separate Supply : The analog section is supplied through its own path, filtered from the digital section, so noise from the digital side does not get into the readings Effect : MAP, TPS, IAT, CLT, O2, Battery, and the spare analog inputs are more stable and consistent — most noticeable on the readings used for fueling decisions No Setup Needed : Everything is on the board; there is no jumper or firmware setting that goes with it Calibration Note : Analog sensor calibrations carried over from a v1.3C board should be rechecked — not necessarily changed, but small offsets that were "compensated" in the calibration tables may no longer be needed
docs.title: More Stable Analog Sensor Readings (New in v1.3D)

docs.text: R13 (120 Ω) : Permanently fitted between CANH (pin 4) and CANL (pin 21). There is no jumper to disconnect it When this is correct : The ECU is at an end of the CAN bus. A healthy CAN bus has exactly two 120 Ω terminators, one at each end CAUTION : If the ECU is installed in the middle of a bus whose two ends are already terminated, the total resistance drops to 40 Ω and the bus may fail to communicate. In that case remove one of the other terminators , or lift R13 off the board Other Mazduino devices : Racedash and the WBO CAN Controller may also carry their own terminators — count the terminators across the whole network, not per device

docs.text: Mazduino Mini 6CH v1.3D is designed around an ARM Cortex-M4 180 MHz as the main MCU, delivering high performance at a 180MHz clock. It supports several add-on modules such as the VR Conditioner Module and the Idle Stepper Module. By default, Mazduino Mini 6CH v1.3D only supports digital CKP and CMP signals, such as hall and optical sensors. Vehicles that still use VR sensors need the VR Module added (or the sensor can be converted to hall). For idle, Mazduino Mini 6CH v1.3D supports Idle PWM, with 2 low-side MOSFET outputs that can be used for IDLE PWM control. Idle Control with a stepper motor requires an add-on module, the Idle Stepper Motor Module. A DRV8825 driver can be used here. On v1.3D, the analog section uses its own reference voltage and a supply path separate from the digital section — both are on the board and need no user configuration. The board also carries a 120 Ω CAN termination resistor. There are solder jumpers on the back of the PCB: v1.3D Solder Jumpers: Tach Pullup: Pullup for the tachometer/RPM Speedometer, using 12V or 5V Ignition VDrive 1-4: Signal voltage for Ignition channels 1, 2, 3, 4 (12V or 5V) Ignition VDrive 5-6: Signal voltage for Ignition channels 5 and 6 (12V or 5V) — separate from the 1-4 jumper Knock/MCU PC13 (JP9): Selects the Knock sensor input or a direct connection to MCU pin PC13. On v1.3D this jumper ships open — neither side is connected at the factory, unlike v1.3C, where the default is Knock JP5: CKP/Primary trigger pullup JP4: CMP/Secondary trigger pullup JP2: VR or Hall option for CKP/Primary JP3: VR or Hall option for CMP/Secondary JP6: Idle Stepper bypass JP7 & JP8: Knock filter bypass Pullup Launch: Pullup on the spare input 3 pin when it is used for a launch control activation button or another input that needs a pullup

docs.text: Mazduino Mini 6CH (v1.4) ¶ Note : v1.4 is not a production version . The last production version of the Mini 6CH line is v1.3D . This page is kept as reference documentation. Overview ¶ The Mazduino Mini 6CH v1.4 is a 6-channel Engine Control Unit with advanced features, designed for use with rusEFI firmware. Built around a powerful 32-bit ARM Cortex-M4 processor, it provides comprehensive engine management with full support for current technologies such as Variable Valve Timing (VVT), Boost Control, and dual Electronic Throttle Body (ETB). New in v1.4: VVT (Variable Valve Timing) : Variable valve timing control for optimal performance and efficiency BOOST Control : Integrated boost pressure control for forced induction applications Dual ETB IC : Dual Electronic Throttle Body support with integrated driver ICs Enhanced Idle Control : Dedicated driver for an Electronic Throttle Body or an Idle Stepper Motor Key Features ¶ Primary trigger input for VR, hall or optical CKP sensors Secondary trigger input for VR, hall or optical CMP sensors 9 analog inputs (0-5V) for MAP, TPS, IAT, CLT, O2, and 4 spares that can be used for a fuel pressure sensor or other sensors 5V sensor power supply with internal fuse protection 4 digital pullup inputs for AC Switch, VSS, Clutch, Launch Control 8x high-current 3A low-side drivers for high-impedance injectors, idle PWM (ISC), Boost, VVT and more 5x low-current low-side drivers for the main relay, fuel pump, AC compressor, fan, and tachometer control 6x 12V or 5V outputs for ignition coil signals Knock Input for engine knock detection VVT Control (v1.4) : Variable Valve Timing control for performance optimization Boost Control (v1.4) : Boost pressure control with precise PWM Dual ETB Support (v1.4) : Dual Electronic Throttle Body support with integrated driver ICs ETB/Stepper Compatibility (v1.4) : The driver can be used for an ETB or an Idle Stepper Motor Support for an add-on VR Conditioner Module 168 MHz ARM Cortex-M4 processor Data communication via CANbus Data communication via USB Type-C Serial RX/TX communication 48-pin automotive connector SD card for data logging Jumper Configuration ¶ The Mazduino Mini 6CH v1.4 has a system of solder jumpers that lets you customize functions to suit your application. These jumpers give configuration flexibility without changing the firmware, ensuring good compatibility with a wide range of engine setups. Top Configuration Zone (Right) ¶ JP11 - Tachometer Pullup ¶ Function : Sets the voltage of the tachometer output signal Options : 12V or 5V Application : Match it to your vehicle's dashboard Ignition VDrive Jumper ¶ Function : Sets the ignition signal voltage for Smart Coil Only Options : 12V or 5V signal Smart Coil only : This jumper is only for smart coils with an internal driver IMPORTANT : Dump coils require an external IGBT Knock/PC13 Input Selection ¶ Knock Mode : Knock sensor input for engine knock detection (default) PC13 Mode : Direct access to the MCU pin for custom functions Enhanced v1.4 : Improved knock detection sensitivity Middle Configuration Zone ¶ JP5 & JP4 - Sensor Pullup Configuration ¶ JP5 : 5V pullup for the CKP (Crankshaft Position) signal JP4 : 5V pullup for the CMP (Camshaft Position) signal Benefit : Clean, stable trigger signals JP2 & JP3 - Sensor Type Selection ¶ JP2 : CKP signal mode (VR or Hall sensor) JP3 : CMP signal mode (VR or Hall sensor) Flexibility : Compatible with many types of position sensors Left Configuration Zone ¶ JP10 - CAN Bus Controller ¶ Function : Enables the TJA1051T/3 CAN bus IC Application : High-speed data communication with other devices Protocol : Supports the automotive CAN 2.0 standard JP6 - ETB/Stepper Motor Mode Selection (New in v1.4) ¶ ETB Mode : Configuration for an Electronic Throttle Body with the integrated driver IC Stepper Mode : Configuration for Idle Stepper Motor control Flexibility : The function can be changed without changing the hardware Default : ETB mode, for modern throttle control applications JP7 & JP8 - Knock Sensor Filter Bypass ¶ Function : Filter bypass for the knock sensor JP7 : Bypasses the knock channel 1 filter JP8 : Bypasses the knock channel 2 filter Advanced Feature : Fine-tuning of knock detection sensitivity Jumper Configuration Tips ¶ Optimal Settings v1.4: ¶ Smart Coils : Use 5V VDrive for coils with a 5V signal and 12V for coils with a 12V signal Dump/Conventional Coils : Require an external IGBT VR Sensors : Select VR mode (the signal goes through the VR Conditioner module) and remove the pullup. The pullup loads the VR sensor coil Hall / Optical Sensors : Select Hall mode and fit the pullup (JP5 for CKP, JP4 for CMP). Hall sensors are usually open-collector and cannot produce a HIGH level on their own; without a pullup the trigger pin floats and picks up noise, which causes trigger errors while the engine is running. Remove the pullup only for sensors with a 5V push-pull output ETB Mode : Select ETB mode for modern electronic throttle applications Stepper Mode : Select stepper mode for conventional idle control Best Practices: ¶ Pre-Installation : Configure the jumpers before final installation Documentation : Write down the jumper configuration for future reference Testing : Verify the signals after changing the jumper configuration Compatibility : Make sure the jumpers match the hardware you are using ETB Testing : Test the ETB driver before connecting the actual throttle body VVT Calibration : Calibrate the VVT system carefully Special Attention: ¶ Coil Type Is Critical : VDrive is only for smart coils; dump coils need an external IGBT ETB Safety : Dual ETB requires a correct failsafe configuration High Current : The VVT and Boost outputs can handle high current; make sure the wiring is adequate Solder Carefully : Use the correct soldering temperature Verify Connections : Make sure the solder joints are solid Consult the Schematic : Refer to the diagram for advanced configuration Power Off : Always switch the power off when changing jumpers Wiring and Installation ¶ Connector docs.text: The Mazduino Mini 6CH v1.4 is a 6-channel Engine Control Unit with advanced features, designed for use with rusEFI firmware. Built around a powerful 32-bit ARM Cortex-M4 processor, it provides comprehensive engine management with full support for current technologies such as Variable Valve Timing (VVT), Boost Control, and dual Electronic Throttle Body (ETB). New in v1.4: VVT (Variable Valve Timing) : Variable valve timing control for optimal performance and efficiency BOOST Control : Integrated boost pressure control for forced induction applications Dual ETB IC : Dual Electronic Throttle Body support with integrated driver ICs Enhanced Idle Control : Dedicated driver for an Electronic Throttle Body or an Idle Stepper Motor
docs.title: Overview

docs.text: Primary trigger input for VR, hall or optical CKP sensors Secondary trigger input for VR, hall or optical CMP sensors 9 analog inputs (0-5V) for MAP, TPS, IAT, CLT, O2, and 4 spares that can be used for a fuel pressure sensor or other sensors 5V sensor power supply with internal fuse protection 4 digital pullup inputs for AC Switch, VSS, Clutch, Launch Control 8x high-current 3A low-side drivers for high-impedance injectors, idle PWM (ISC), Boost, VVT and more 5x low-current low-side drivers for the main relay, fuel pump, AC compressor, fan, and tachometer control 6x 12V or 5V outputs for ignition coil signals Knock Input for engine knock detection VVT Control (v1.4) : Variable Valve Timing control for performance optimization Boost Control (v1.4) : Boost pressure control with precise PWM Dual ETB Support (v1.4) : Dual Electronic Throttle Body support with integrated driver ICs ETB/Stepper Compatibility (v1.4) : The driver can be used for an ETB or an Idle Stepper Motor Support for an add-on VR Conditioner Module 168 MHz ARM Cortex-M4 processor Data communication via CANbus Data communication via USB Type-C Serial RX/TX communication 48-pin automotive connector SD card for data logging

docs.text: Smart Coils : Use 5V VDrive for coils with a 5V signal and 12V for coils with a 12V signal Dump/Conventional Coils : Require an external IGBT VR Sensors : Select VR mode (the signal goes through the VR Conditioner module) and remove the pullup. The pullup loads the VR sensor coil Hall / Optical Sensors : Select Hall mode and fit the pullup (JP5 for CKP, JP4 for CMP). Hall sensors are usually open-collector and cannot produce a HIGH level on their own; without a pullup the trigger pin floats and picks up noise, which causes trigger errors while the engine is running. docs.text: Mazduino Racedash Pro ¶ Overview ¶ Racedash Pro M4 (4.3"): eight shift light LEDs above the screen, with Template 1 and a "Start Engine" switch from the Switch Panel Mazduino Racedash Pro is the digital dash display variant with a larger screen, available in 4.3", 5" and 7" . Unlike the Mazduino Racedash variants (3.5" and 4"), which are configured over WiFi and a browser, the Racedash Pro can be set up directly on the screen (touchscreen) without connecting to a phone/laptop. The DashTune Android app is also available over Bluetooth for settings that are not in the on-screen menu. Variant Screen Size Connector Racedash Pro 4.3" (M4) 4.3 inch DTM4 (Deutsch DTM 4 Pin) Racedash Pro 5" (M5) 5 inch DTM4 (Deutsch DTM 4 Pin) Racedash Pro 7" (M7) 7 inch DTM4 (Deutsch DTM 4 Pin) Key Features ¶ Touchscreen, so the dashboard can be set up directly on the screen, with no extra app or WiFi connection Shows RPM, gear indicator, speed and other sensor data in real time Communicates with the ECU over CAN Bus or Serial , depending on the ECU used. Speeduino -based ECUs use Serial mode, while rusEFI , Haltech and MaxxECU use CAN Bus mode Vehicles without a CAN bus can use the M-Link protocol together with the CAN IO Extender , which reads sensors, switches and RPM and sends them to the dash DTM4 / 4 Pin Connector ¶ The Racedash Pro uses the same DTM4 (Deutsch DTM 4 Pin) connector as the Racedash 4" variant, in both the physical connector and the pin functions. Dash connector side Cable connector side Pin No. Description 1 12V Power Supply 2 Ground 3 CAN High / TX 4 CAN Low / RX Note: Pins 3 and 4 work as CAN High/CAN Low for rusEFI , Haltech and MaxxECU ECUs (CAN Bus mode). For Speeduino ECUs only, pins 3 and 4 work as Serial TX/RX , because Speeduino has no native CAN Bus. Racedash Pro M4 / M5 / M7 ¶ This section covers the M4 (4.3"), M5 (5") and M7 (7"). The connector and wiring are exactly the same as described in DTM4 / 4 Pin Connector above. Racedash Pro M7 (7"): front view powered on, front view, rear side with its mount, and side view Rear side with the connector fitted Supported ECUs ¶ ECU Connection Notes rusEFI CAN Bus 500 kbps Most complete data Haltech CAN Bus 1 Mbps The only one that sends turn signal, handbrake and tire pressure data MaxxECU CAN Bus 500 kbps Speeduino Serial Speeduino has no CAN, so pins 3 and 4 are used as TX/RX OBD-II CAN Bus (ISO 15765-4) For the car's stock factory ECU, read the limitations The ECU type is selected in the DashTune app or in the on-screen menu, and no firmware change is needed . The CAN speed follows the selected ECU automatically. Besides rusEFI, Haltech, MaxxECU, Speeduino and OBD-II in this table, the Racedash Pro also supports ECUMASTER EMU Black and Link Generic Dash . What has to be enabled on each ECU is covered in ECU Configuration for Racedash . Data shown for all ECUs: RPM, MAP, TPS, ignition timing, injector duty, AFR/lambda, pressures and temperatures (coolant, oil, fuel, intake air), EGT 1–4, gear, ethanol content and battery voltage. Note : The turn signal , handbrake and tire pressure lights only come on with Haltech , because only Haltech sends that data. On rusEFI and MaxxECU these three lights will never come on; this is not a fault. OBD-II Limitations ¶ Not every OBD-II car can be read by this dash, and we do not guarantee that your car is one that can. Check the following before buying for OBD-II use. Only OBD-II over CAN Bus is supported, that is ISO 15765-4 with 11-bit identifiers , at 500 kbps . Not supported: Protocol Description ISO 9141-2 K-line, common on older cars ISO 14230-4 (KWP2000) K-line SAE J1850 PWM / VPW Common on older American cars ISO 15765-4 29-bit identifier CAN variant used by some vehicles In general, cars built from 2008 onward in many markets already use OBD-II over CAN, but this is not a guarantee: the changeover year differs between brands and countries. Even when the protocol matches, the data shown depends on what your car responds to . The dash first asks which PIDs are supported, then only reads the ones that are answered. The PIDs read are: RPM, speed, TPS, MAP, coolant temperature, intake air temperature, voltage and oil temperature. Many cars do not answer some of these; oil temperature is among the ones most often unavailable. OBD-II is also slower than the dedicated CAN protocols of standalone ECUs, because the dash has to ask and then wait for an answer for each value, instead of receiving periodic broadcasts. Changing the display (template) ¶ The dash offers several dashboard displays. To switch, swipe left or right on the top part of the screen (in the RPM bar area). The bottom part of the screen deliberately ignores swipes so that the switches there are not touched by accident. The last display used is remembered, so when powered on again the dash opens the same display straight away. Some example displays on the Racedash Pro M7: The gauge colors and the content of each panel can be changed, so the display on your dash may differ from the examples above. On-screen menu (M4 / M5 / M7) ¶ Screen gestures ¶ Gesture Result Swipe left / right on the RPM bar (top part of the screen) Change the dashboard display Swipe up Open the Switch Panel Two-finger pinch Open the main menu Swipes are only picked up on the top part of the screen. The bottom part is deliberately left free so that switches placed there are not touched by accident when changing displays. Main menu, opened with a two-finger pinch Switch Panel, opened by swiping up Menu structure ¶ Menu ├── Dash → back to the last dashboard ├── Switch Panel → Switch Panel page └── Setting ├── Display Setting → choose a template, then set the content of each panel ├── General Setting → units, maximum RPM, range of each data item └── CAN ├── Protocol → choose the ECU type └── Switch Panel → create and edit switches Display Setting: setting the content of each template ¶ Menu → Setting → Display Setting , then choose the template you want to change (Template 1 to Template 5). The content of each data box on the template can be changed, for example from oil pressure to gearbox temperature, with the left/right arrow buttons. Press Save to save, or Discard to cancel. The settings are stored on the dash and are not lost when the engine is switched off. Note for the M7 : Template 3 on the M7 has fixed content, so choosing it in Display Setting opens its display directly, not the settings page. General Setting: units and data ranges ¶ Menu → Setting → General Setting : Pressure unit : kPa or PSI Temperature unit : °C or °F Maximum RPM : the full scale of every RPM gauge, adjusted up and down in 250 RPM steps; the redline is set automatically at about 5/6 of this number Data Source : a list of all data sources. Choose one to set its minimum and maximum values , which set the gauge range and the min/max numbers printed on the screen Changes to the units and maximum RPM show up right away on every template. CAN: ECU type and Switch Panel ¶ Menu → Setting → CAN contains two things: Protocol : selects the ECU type (rusEFI, Haltech, MaxxECU, Speeduino, OBD-II). The CAN speed adjusts itself. No firmware change and no restart needed : once saved, the dash reads with the new protocol right away. Switch Panel : create and edit switches: name, CAN ID and the data that is sent. Switches you create appear on the Switch Panel page. Menu → Setting → CAN → Protocol Switch Panel ¶ Swipe up from the dashboard to open the Switch Panel . This page is used to send commands to the ECU or other devices on the CAN network, for example turning on a fan or nitrous, or triggering launch control, just by pressing a switch on the screen. Press DASHBOARD to go back to the dashboard. The Switch Panel can also be made a tile on the main menu through Setting → Menu . Switches can be set up on the screen (Setting → CAN → Switch Panel) or in the DashTune app. There are two kinds of switch: SWITCH : press once for ON, press again for OFF. While ON, the dash keeps sending the ON command. Formerly called Toggle. PUSH : sends the command once each time it is pressed. Formerly called Momentary. On a Racedash Pro with the latest firmware, each switch has three extra settings. All three are set in DashTune: Switch Panel , then edit the switch. Icon : choose from a list of automotive icons, for example engine, fan, nitrous, launch, anti-lag, turbo, lights, horn, A/C and wiper. The icon is shown on the switch card on the dash and in the app. Hold to activate : off, 0.5, 1, 2 or 3 seconds. The switch only acts after being pressed for that long; while it is held, a bar fills along the bottom of the card. This setting prevents a switch from being pressed by accident on bumpy roads. Turning off a switch that is ON does not need to be held. Stay ON after power-off (SWITCH type only): off by default, meaning every switch starts OFF each time the dash powers on. This is safer for nitrous, anti-lag and launch. Turn this setting on per switch if that switch really should come back ON. Change for existing owners : before this update, a switch left ON would come back ON after the dash was switched off and on again. Now every switch starts OFF, except switches whose Stay ON after power-off setting is turned on. Other settings only in DashTune ¶ Some settings are not available in the on-screen menu and can only be changed in the app: MAP display : Absolute (the number as is, about 101 kPa at idle) or Boost (calculated from the outside air pressure, so under vacuum the number is negative and 0 means no boost yet) Splash duration at power-on GPS module : only for units that actually have a GPS module fitted The GPS module is optional and is not included in the unit as sold. The Racedash Pro ships without a GPS module, so this setting does not need to be turned on for a standard unit. The GPS module is only fitted on special request when ordering. Without that module, speed data is still read from the ECU as usual. The splash and GPS settings only take effect after the dash is switched off and on again. Indicator lights ¶ The warning lights come on automatically: Light Comes on when Check engine The ECU reports a fault code Battery Voltage outside 11.5–15.5 V Coolant temperature Above 105 °C Oil temperature Above 130 °C Oil pressure Engine running (above 800 RPM) but pressure below 100 kPa Left/right turn signal, handbrake, tire pressure Haltech only All lights go out if the connection to the ECU is lost, so no light stays on after the ignition key is switched off. For ECUs other than Haltech, the turn signal, handbrake, high beam and parking light indicators can still be driven from the vehicle's switches by adding the CAN IO Extender . DashTune App Guide ¶ DashTune is an Android app for setting up the dash from your phone. For the Racedash Pro M4/M5/M7, it connects over Bluetooth : no WiFi needed and nothing to unplug. Getting the app: DashTune is still in testing. Open www.mazduino.com/dashtune/tester on your Android phone and follow the three steps with the same Google account that is active in the Play Store: join the tester group, tap Become a tester , then install DashTune from the Play Store. If the Play Store shows "Can't download DashTune" ¶ This message usually appears right after tapping Install or Update , before the download has started. The cause is in the Play Store on the phone, not in the app. Open Settings → Apps → Google Play Store → Storage , then tap Clear cache (not Clear storage). Open the Play Store again, find DashTune, and tap Install once more. If it still fails, make sure the Google account active in the Play Store (the profile picture at the top right) is the account whose email was registered for DashTune testing. If the phone has several accounts, switch to that one. A newly released version is sometimes not ready to download for a few minutes. If the steps above have not worked, wait a moment and try again. If it still fails, contact support@mazduino.com with your phone model and the email of the Play Store account you are using. Connecting for the first time ¶ Turn the ignition key on until the dash powers up. Open DashTune, go to the Device tab, tap Add Dash . Tap Scan . The dash will appear by itself. Select that dash. Once connected, the app opens the menu page straight away. If it is not found: make sure the phone's Bluetooth is on, the dash is powered on, and the dash is not connected to another phone. You can also choose the model manually under Dash model on the same screen. A dash that has been connected before is remembered, and the app connects by itself the next time it is opened. DashTune menu contents ¶ Left: the DashTune home screen while connected to a Racedash Pro M7. Right: the dash screen with the Apex theme. Order of the menus on the DashTune home screen: Menu Function Themes Choose the theme shown on the dash and install new themes from the Theme Store. On old firmware this menu is called Dashboard and sets the data shown on each template Switch Panel Create and set up the switches shown on the dash's Switch Panel. On old firmware this menu is called CAN Buttons General Setting Units, MAP mode, maximum RPM, range of each data item: the same as the menu on the dash screen Data log Records trip data to the dash's memory. When the memory is full, the oldest log is deleted. To retrieve logs, the phone connects briefly to the dash's WiFi LED lights Shift light and indicators, only on dashes that have an LED strip Splash Create your own opening image (see below) Update Firmware Updates the dash firmware. At the bottom is WiFi OTA Mode , which turns on the dash's WiFi so it can be reached from a computer Info Firmware version and device status Themes and Theme Store ¶ Open Themes to see the themes on the dash and choose the one to show. The Apex theme is always installed by default. Tap Theme Store to see other themes with their previews, then choose a theme and tap Install . During installation the phone briefly joins the dash's Mazduino-Dash WiFi; the dashboard keeps running as usual. General Setting and Switch Panel ¶ In General Setting , the ECU protocol is changed directly without reflashing the firmware. This is also where you find the pressure and temperature units, MAP mode, screen brightness, Max RPM, the range of each data item, Custom Channels, the fuel level source and the source of each indicator. Switch Panel holds the switches shown on the dash screen; tap the pencil icon to edit a switch, or + to add a new switch. Icon, Hold to activate and Stay ON after power-off are set here (see Switch Panel ). Settings history is in the More → Account tab. It stores the dash settings over time. Check its contents first, then choose the one you want to restore to the dash. Making your own splash screen ¶ Go to the Splash menu. There you can add images from the gallery, add text, move and resize, then choose the background color. When finished, tap send. Because the image is sent over WiFi, the dash automatically turns on its own WiFi for a moment, the phone switches to it, the image is sent, then the phone returns to the original network. The process runs by itself: just keep the phone screen on and do not close the app until it finishes. There is also a splash display duration setting, and a button to delete it and go back to the default image. If sending the splash fails or the splash disappears ¶ On the Racedash Pro M4, M4.1, M5, M5.1, M5.2 and M7 with firmware before 6 November 2026, the dash storage could jam after the splash, template or animation was changed a few times. The M7 Pro is not affected by this problem. Symptoms: Sending the splash fails, for example with "connection reset by peer" or "The dash could not save the file" . The old splash is lost as well, so the dash powers on without an opening image. How to fix it: Update the DashTune app to version 1.2.11 or newer. Update the dash firmware through the Update Firmware menu to version 2026-11-06 or newer. The firmware update still works even when sending the splash fails. Send the splash again. The first send after the update can take about one minute longer, because the dash tidies up its storage first. Keep the phone screen on and the app open until it finishes. From that firmware on, the old splash is no longer deleted if sending fails. If the file really is too large, DashTune shows "Not enough room on the dash" ; delete unused themes or animations, or shorten the splash, then try again. If the phone is already on the Mazduino-Dash WiFi but you get "connection timed out" or a message that the dash cannot be reached, first turn off any VPN or ad-blocking app on the phone. Apps like these redirect the connection so it does not reach the dash. If it still fails, contact support@mazduino.com with the dash model, the firmware version (Setting > About) and the error message shown. Update firmware ¶ Go to the Update Firmware menu; the app checks for the latest version and shows the version currently installed. If there is a new version, tap the update button. Warning : Do not update while driving. During the update the dash screen goes off for a while, then comes back on by itself. Make sure the vehicle is in a safe state, the power is not cut, and the app is not closed until it finishes. An update that is interrupted partway can leave the dash unable to start. Relay features: Google Maps and music ¶ DashTune can forward Google Maps directions and the song currently playing on the phone to the dash screen. The settings are in the More → Relay tab. The dash does not play music. Music is still played from the phone, or from a head unit connected to the phone. The Phone music page on the dash only shows the song title, artist and cover, plus play, pause and skip buttons to control the phone. The PHONE MUSIC tile can be shown through Setting → Menu . This feature needs notification access permission on the phone, and the app will take you to its settings page the first time it is enabled. References ¶ Mazduino website - https://www.mazduino.com/ Mazduino Wiki - https://wiki.mazduino.com/ Mazduino Github - https://github.com/mazduino/mazduino

docs.text: ECU Connection Notes rusEFI CAN Bus 500 kbps Most complete data Haltech CAN Bus 1 Mbps The only one that sends turn signal, handbrake and tire pressure data MaxxECU CAN Bus 500 kbps Speeduino Serial Speeduino has no CAN, so pins 3 and 4 are used as TX/RX OBD-II CAN Bus (ISO 15765-4) For the car's stock factory ECU, read the limitations The ECU type is selected in the DashTune app or in the on-screen menu, and no firmware change is needed . The CAN speed follows the selected ECU automatically. Besides rusEFI, Haltech, MaxxECU, Speeduino and OBD-II in this table, the Racedash Pro also supports ECUMASTER EMU Black and Link Generic Dash . What has to be enabled on each ECU is covered in ECU Configuration for Racedash . Data shown for all ECUs: RPM, MAP, TPS, ignition timing, injector duty, AFR/lambda, pressures and temperatures (coolant, oil, fuel, intake air), EGT 1–4, gear, ethanol content and battery voltage. Note : The turn signal , handbrake and tire pressure lights only come on with Haltech , because only Haltech sends that data. On rusEFI and MaxxECU these three lights will never come on; this is not a fault.
docs.title: Supported ECUs

docs.text: Not every OBD-II car can be read by this dash, and we do not guarantee that your car is one that can. Check the following before buying for OBD-II use. Only OBD-II over CAN Bus is supported, that is ISO 15765-4 with 11-bit identifiers , at 500 kbps . Not supported: Protocol Description ISO 9141-2 K-line, common on older cars ISO 14230-4 (KWP2000) K-line SAE J1850 PWM / VPW Common on older American cars ISO 15765-4 29-bit identifier CAN variant used by some vehicles In general, cars built from 2008 onward in many markets already use OBD-II over CAN, but this is not a guarantee: the changeover year differs between brands and countries. Even when the protocol matches, the data shown depends on what your car responds to . The dash first asks which PIDs are supported, then only reads the ones that are answered. The PIDs read are: RPM, speed, TPS, MAP, coolant temperature, intake air temperature, voltage and oil temperature. Many cars do not answer some of these; oil temperature is among the ones most often unavailable. OBD-II is also slower than the dedicated CAN protocols of standalone ECUs, because the dash has to ask and then wait for an answer for each value, instead of receiving periodic broadcasts.
docs.title: OBD-II Limitations

docs.text: The dash offers several dashboard displays. To switch, swipe left or right on the top part of the screen (in the RPM bar area). The bottom part of the screen deliberately ignores swipes so that the switches there are not touched by accident. The last display used is remembered, so when powered on again the dash opens the same display straight away. Some example displays on the Racedash Pro M7: The gauge colors and the content of each panel can be changed, so the display on your dash may differ from the examples above.

docs.text: Menu → Setting → Display Setting , then choose the template you want to change (Template 1 to Template 5). The content of each data box on the template can be changed, for example from oil pressure to gearbox temperature, with the left/right arrow buttons. Press Save to save, or Discard to cancel. The settings are stored on the dash and are not lost when the engine is switched off. Note for the M7 : Template 3 on the M7 has fixed content, so choosing it in Display Setting opens its display directly, not the settings page.
docs.title: Display Setting: setting the content of each template

docs.text: Menu → Setting → General Setting : Pressure unit : kPa or PSI Temperature unit : °C or °F Maximum RPM : the full scale of every RPM gauge, adjusted up and down in 250 RPM steps; the redline is set automatically at about 5/6 of this number Data Source : a list of all data sources. Choose one to set its minimum and maximum values , which set the gauge range and the min/max numbers printed on the screen Changes to the units and maximum RPM show up right away on every template.
docs.title: General Setting: units and data ranges

docs.text: Menu → Setting → CAN contains two things: Protocol : selects the ECU type (rusEFI, Haltech, MaxxECU, Speeduino, OBD-II). The CAN speed adjusts itself. No firmware change and no restart needed : once saved, the dash reads with the new protocol right away. Switch Panel : create and edit switches: name, CAN ID and the data that is sent. Switches you create appear on the Switch Panel page. Menu → Setting → CAN → Protocol
docs.title: CAN: ECU type and Switch Panel

docs.text: Swipe up from the dashboard to open the Switch Panel . This page is used to send commands to the ECU or other devices on the CAN network, for example turning on a fan or nitrous, or triggering launch control, just by pressing a switch on the screen. Press DASHBOARD to go back to the dashboard. The Switch Panel can also be made a tile on the main menu through Setting → Menu . Switches can be set up on the screen (Setting → CAN → Switch Panel) or in the DashTune app. There are two kinds of switch: SWITCH : press once for ON, press again for OFF. While ON, the dash keeps sending the ON command. Formerly called Toggle. PUSH : sends the command once each time it is pressed. Formerly called Momentary. On a Racedash Pro with the latest firmware, each switch has three extra settings. All three are set in DashTune: Switch Panel , then edit the switch. Icon : choose from a list of automotive icons, for example engine, fan, nitrous, launch, anti-lag, turbo, lights, horn, A/C and wiper. The icon is shown on the switch card on the dash and in the app. Hold to activate : off, 0.5, 1, 2 or 3 seconds. The switch only acts after being pressed for that long; while it is held, a bar fills along the bottom of the card. This setting prevents a switch from being pressed by accident on bumpy roads. Turning off a switch that is ON does not need to be held. Stay ON after power-off (SWITCH type only): off by default, meaning every switch starts OFF each time the dash powers on. This is safer for nitrous, anti-lag and launch. Turn this setting on per switch if that switch really should come back ON. Change for existing owners : before this update, a switch left ON would come back ON after the dash was switched off and on again. Now every switch starts OFF, except switches whose Stay ON after power-off setting is turned on.
docs.title: Switch Panel

docs.text: Some settings are not available in the on-screen menu and can only be changed in the app: MAP display : Absolute (the number as is, about 101 kPa at idle) or Boost (calculated from the outside air pressure, so under vacuum the number is negative and 0 means no boost yet) Splash duration at power-on GPS module : only for units that actually have a GPS module fitted The GPS module is optional and is not included in the unit as sold. The Racedash Pro ships without a GPS module, so this setting does not need to be turned on for a standard unit. The GPS module is only fitted on special request when ordering. Without that module, speed data is still read from the ECU as usual. The splash and GPS settings only take effect after the dash is switched off and on again.
docs.title: Other settings only in DashTune

docs.text: The warning lights come on automatically: Light Comes on when Check engine The ECU reports a fault code Battery Voltage outside 11.5–15.5 V Coolant temperature Above 105 °C Oil temperature Above 130 °C Oil pressure Engine running (above 800 RPM) but pressure below 100 kPa Left/right turn signal, handbrake, tire pressure Haltech only All lights go out if the connection to the ECU is lost, so no light stays on after the ignition key is switched off. For ECUs other than Haltech, the turn signal, handbrake, high beam and parking light indicators can still be driven from the vehicle's switches by adding the CAN IO Extender .

docs.text: Mazduino Racedash ¶ Overview ¶ Mazduino Racedash is a digital dash display that shows real-time data from the ECU, such as RPM, gear indicator, speed and other sensor data. This page covers the 3.5" and 4" screen variants. For the larger screen variants (4.3", 5" and 7"), see Mazduino Racedash Pro . Variant Screen Size Connector Racedash 3.5" 3.5 inch JST 4 Pin Racedash 4" (Cabus) 4 inch DTM4 (Deutsch DTM 4 Pin) Both variants are set up from a phone with the DashTune app, over the WiFi network that the dash broadcasts. Go straight to Setting Up with DashTune . The DashTune home page while connected to the dash. Key Features ¶ Digital screen showing RPM, gear indicator, speed and other sensor data in real time Set up from the DashTune Android app: screen template, data in each panel, indicator lights, ECU protocol, splash screen and firmware updates, all from your phone Two screen templates: Classic (RPM bar, gear, speed and boxed panels) and Grid (one full screen of data panels) Communicates with the ECU over CAN Bus or Serial , depending on what was requested when ordering and on the ECU used. Speeduino -based ECUs must use Serial mode (for both the JST 4 Pin and DTM4 variants), while rusEFI , Haltech and MaxxECU use CAN Bus mode The ECU side must be set up too. The dash only listens: the ECU has to broadcast its data, at the right CAN speed. See ECU Configuration for Racedash . Racedash 3.5" (JST 4 Pin Connector) ¶ This variant uses a compact JST 4 Pin connector for quick installation. There is no USB port exposed outside the case: firmware updates are done over WiFi, see Update Firmware . JST 4 Pin Connector (Wiring to the Vehicle) ¶ The external connector used to connect the Racedash to the vehicle/ECU. Pin Function 1 12V 2 GND 3 RX / CANL 4 TX / CANH Racedash 4" / Cabus (DTM4 Connector) ¶ Racedash 4" powered on: RPM bar, gear indicator and the row of warning lights below the screen This variant uses a DTM4 (Deutsch DTM 4 Pin) connector that resists vibration and weather, suited to racing use. It communicates with the ECU over CAN Bus , except with Speeduino ECUs, which use Serial mode (the secondary serial port of the Arduino Mega). DTM4 / 4 Pin Connector ¶ Dash connector side Cable connector side Pin No. Description 1 12V Power Supply 2 Ground 3 CAN High / TX 4 CAN Low / RX Note: Pins 3 and 4 work as CAN High/CAN Low for rusEFI , Haltech and MaxxECU ECUs (CAN Bus mode). For Speeduino ECUs only, pins 3 and 4 work as Serial TX/RX : Speeduino has no native CAN Bus, so the data is read from the secondary serial port (Serial3) of the Arduino Mega . Setting Up with DashTune ¶ DashTune is the official Android app for setting up the Racedash. Everything that used to be set up in the browser (Display Control) and in the Splash Screen Generator is now in one app, and it works without an internet connection as long as the phone is connected to the dash's WiFi. The Racedash 3.5" and 4" connect to DashTune over WiFi . The Racedash Pro (M4/M5/M7) uses Bluetooth; its guide is on the Racedash Pro page. 1. Install DashTune ¶ DashTune is still in testing, so it is installed through the Google Play tester program. Open www.mazduino.com/dashtune/tester on your Android phone, then follow the three steps there with the same Google account that is active in the Play Store: Join the DashTune tester group. Tap Become a tester on the Google Play tester page. Install DashTune from the Play Store. If the Play Store shows "Can't download DashTune" , see how to fix it . 2. Connect to the dash ¶ Turn on the dash, then connect the phone's WiFi to "MAZDUINO_Display" with the password "12345678" . If Android asks because this WiFi network has no internet, choose to stay connected. Open DashTune, go to the Device tab, then tap Add Dash . Tap Scan . The dash will be found on the WiFi network the phone is currently using. If it is not found, choose your Racedash model under Dash model , enter IP address 192.168.4.1 (port 80 ), then tap Connect . Once connected, the dash appears on the Home tab as a set of menu cards: Display Control, Data Sources, CAN protocol, Splash, Update Firmware and Info. 3. Display Control ¶ Everything shown on the screen is set here, and sent to the dash right away. Backlight brightness : 0 = off, 255 = brightest. Main screen template : Classic (RPM bar, gear, speed, boxed panels) or Grid (one full screen, one cell per data panel). Indicator row (Classic): Always on : the eight status lights are always visible. Notifications + fuel bar : a light appears for a few seconds when it changes, and the other half of the row becomes a fuel level bar. Indicators : turn each light on or off: SYNC, FAN, ASE, WUE, REV, LCH, AC, DFCO, FPMP, CEL, FAN2, KNOCK, TC, ANTL, SCUT. Turning a light off only hides it on the screen, whether or not the ECU sends it. RPM bar scale : the maximum RPM of the on-screen bar, 1000–20000. RPM shift light : the LED strip above the screen: Light-up RPM , LED brightness , the RPM bar pattern (Mode 1–4), and a Test LEDs button to try it without revving the engine. The RPM shift light settings only appear on dashes that actually have the LED strip. 4. Data Sources ¶ The Racedash has 8 data panels . Tap a panel to choose the data it shows, for example AFR, TPS, IAT, MAP, Coolant, Voltage or ADV. Choose Disabled to leave the panel empty. 5. CAN Protocol ¶ This menu shows the ECU protocol the dash reads and its CAN bitrate. The firmware of the Racedash 3.5" and 4" (M1, M2, M3, C1) is built for one ECU, as ordered, so only that ECU's protocol and Custom can be selected here. This is different from the Racedash Pro (M4, M5, M7, M7 Pro), whose protocol can be changed directly in the settings. Custom is used for ECUs that are not on the list, with a CAN data map you set up yourself. If the car's ECU is changed to another brand, the dash does not need to be sent back: open Update Firmware and choose Flash a different protocol . DashTune asks for confirmation before flashing. This option is only on CAN Bus mode dashes; Serial mode dashes for Speeduino do not use this menu. Also make sure the ECU is already broadcasting its CAN data; see ECU Configuration for Racedash . 6. Splash Screen ¶ The splash is the opening image shown when the dash first powers on. The splash is made directly in DashTune; there is no need to open the Splash Screen Generator on the web any more. Open the Splash card on the Home tab. Tap + Image to place a photo or logo from the phone's gallery, and + Text to write text. You can use more than one layer, for example a background image with a logo on top. Tap a layer to select it, drag to move it, and pinch to make it larger or smaller. For text, set its content, size and font. The background color is chosen from the row of colors below the preview. Tap Send to Dash . Turn the dash off and on again (disconnect power) to see the new splash. To go back to the default splash, tap Delete splash (revert to default) . 7. Update Firmware ¶ Open the Update Firmware card. DashTune checks for the latest version for your dash and shows the version currently installed. Update from Server : downloads and installs the latest version. Because the dash's WiFi has no internet, DashTune downloads over mobile data , so turn on mobile data before you start. Pick Firmware File : installs a firmware file that is already on the phone, for example a file sent by the support team. Flash a different protocol : switches the firmware to another ECU (see CAN Protocol ). If there is no mobile data, download the firmware first while the phone has internet: leave the dash's WiFi, open the Device tab, tap the ⋮ menu on the dash, then Download firmware . After that, reconnect to the dash's WiFi and open Update Firmware to flash the saved file. Warning : Do not update while driving. Make sure the dash's power is not cut and the app is not closed until the process finishes. An update that is interrupted partway can leave the dash unable to start. Ask Dina ¶ The Ask Dina button on the Home tab opens the assistant inside DashTune. Ask anything about installing and setting up the dash, for example "why doesn't RPM show up?". Update Firmware ¶ The recommended way is through DashTune; see Update Firmware in DashTune . Two other methods still work: Mazduino Flasher (laptop, over WiFi) : no need to open the case. USB : open the Racedash case, then connect the internal USB TTL port/pins directly to a computer. With Mazduino Flasher ¶ First log in to your Mazduino account at mazduino.com , then open mazduino.com/dashboard/flasher . Select the OTA (WiFi) tab. Connect the laptop to the "MAZDUINO_Display" WiFi network broadcast by the Racedash, or make sure the Racedash is on the same WiFi network. Select the matching Racedash model under Select Device ( make sure the right device is selected ), then click Start Flashing . Wait for flashing to finish. The process history can be seen under Flash History . Old method: browser and the 192.168.4.1 page ¶ Before DashTune, the Racedash was set up in a browser. This method is still available for those who cannot use DashTune yet (for example, if you only have an iPhone or a laptop), but new features are only added to DashTune. Display Control on mazduino.com (click to open) Before switching WiFi, open a browser and go to https://www.mazduino.com/display-control first, while the phone/laptop is still connected to the internet. Once the page is open, connect the phone/laptop's WiFi to "MAZDUINO_Display" , broadcast by the Racedash, with the password "12345678" . The internet connection will drop, but the page that is already open can still be used. Wait until the Racedash is detected automatically in the Network Scanner . If it is not detected automatically, enter the Racedash IP manually in the Manual IP Address field: 192.168.4.1 , then click Test Connection . Once connected, the Display Control page shows the device information and the CAN Bus/ECU data in real time. Set the data shown in each panel position, the screen template, brightness and the communication mode (CAN Bus/Serial) as needed in the Display Configuration section. Splash Screen Generator on mazduino.com (click to open) Open mazduino.com/splash-generator in a phone/laptop browser. Create the splash screen you want by following the instructions on that page. Upload the result to the Racedash over the "MAZDUINO_Display" WiFi connection. Old firmware: configuration at 192.168.4.1 (click to open) This section only applies to old firmware versions, which still use the local configuration page at 192.168.4.1 . If your Racedash already runs the latest firmware, use DashTune and skip this section. Connect the phone/laptop to the "MAZDUINO_Display" WiFi network with the password "12345678" . Once connected, open a browser and go to http://192.168.4.1 . Set the data shown in each panel position as needed. For the larger screen variants (4.3", 5" and 7"), see Mazduino Racedash Pro . References ¶ Mazduino website - https://www.mazduino.com/ Mazduino Wiki - https://wiki.mazduino.com/ Mazduino Github - https://github.com/mazduino/mazduino Schematics and other supporting files are available on the Mazduino website.

Mazduino Racedash is a digital dash display that shows real-time data from the ECU, such as RPM, gear indicator, speed and other sensor data. This page covers the 3.5" and 4" screen variants. For the larger screen variants (4.3", 5" and 7"), see Mazduino Racedash Pro . Variant Screen Size Connector Racedash 3.5" 3.5 inch JST 4 Pin Racedash 4" (Cabus) 4 inch DTM4 (Deutsch DTM 4 Pin) Both variants are set up from a phone with the DashTune app, over the WiFi network that the dash broadcasts. Go straight to Setting Up with DashTune . The DashTune home page while connected to the dash.
docs.title: Overview

docs.text: Digital screen showing RPM, gear indicator, speed and other sensor data in real time Set up from the DashTune Android app: screen template, data in each panel, indicator lights, ECU protocol, splash screen and firmware updates, all from your phone Two screen templates: Classic (RPM bar, gear, speed and boxed panels) and Grid (one full screen of data panels) Communicates with the ECU over CAN Bus or Serial , depending on what was requested when ordering and on the ECU used. Speeduino -based ECUs must use Serial mode (for both the JST 4 Pin and DTM4 variants), while rusEFI , Haltech and MaxxECU use CAN Bus mode The ECU side must be set up too. The dash only listens: the ECU has to broadcast its data, at the right CAN speed. See ECU Configuration for Racedash .

docs.text: This variant uses a compact JST 4 Pin connector for quick installation. There is no USB port exposed outside the case: firmware updates are done over WiFi, see Update Firmware .

docs.text: Racedash 4" powered on: RPM bar, gear indicator and the row of warning lights below the screen This variant uses a DTM4 (Deutsch DTM 4 Pin) connector that resists vibration and weather, suited to racing use. It communicates with the ECU over CAN Bus , except with Speeduino ECUs, which use Serial mode (the secondary serial port of the Arduino Mega).
docs.title: Racedash 4" / Cabus (DTM4 Connector)

docs.text: Dash connector side Cable connector side Pin No. Description 1 12V Power Supply 2 Ground 3 CAN High / TX 4 CAN Low / RX Note: Pins 3 and 4 work as CAN High/CAN Low for rusEFI , Haltech and MaxxECU ECUs (CAN Bus mode). For Speeduino ECUs only, pins 3 and 4 work as Serial TX/RX : Speeduino has no native CAN Bus, so the data is read from the secondary serial port (Serial3) of the Arduino Mega .

docs.text: DashTune is the official Android app for setting up the Racedash. Everything that used to be set up in the browser (Display Control) and in the Splash Screen Generator is now in one app, and it works without an internet connection as long as the phone is connected to the dash's WiFi. The Racedash 3.5" and 4" connect to DashTune over WiFi . The Racedash Pro (M4/M5/M7) uses Bluetooth; its guide is on the Racedash Pro page.

docs.text: DashTune is still in testing, so it is installed through the Google Play tester program. Open www.mazduino.com/dashtune/tester on your Android phone, then follow the three steps there with the same Google account that is active in the Play Store: Join the DashTune tester group. Tap Become a tester on the Google Play tester page. Install DashTune from the Play Store. If the Play Store shows "Can't download DashTune" , see how to fix it .

docs.text: Turn on the dash, then connect the phone's WiFi to "MAZDUINO_Display" with the password "12345678" . If Android asks because this WiFi network has no internet, choose to stay connected. Open DashTune, go to the Device tab, then tap Add Dash . Tap Scan . The dash will be found on the WiFi network the phone is currently using. If it is not found, choose your Racedash model under Dash model , enter IP address 192.168.4.1 (port 80 ), then tap Connect . Once connected, the dash appears on the Home tab as a set of menu cards: Display Control, Data Sources, CAN protocol, Splash, Update Firmware and Info.

docs.text: Everything shown on the screen is set here, and sent to the dash right away. Backlight brightness : 0 = off, 255 = brightest. Main screen template : Classic (RPM bar, gear, speed, boxed panels) or Grid (one full screen, one cell per data panel). Indicator row (Classic): Always on : the eight status lights are always visible. Notifications + fuel bar : a light appears for a few seconds when it changes, and the other half of the row becomes a fuel level bar. Indicators : turn each light on or off: SYNC, FAN, ASE, WUE, REV, LCH, AC, DFCO, FPMP, CEL, FAN2, KNOCK, TC, ANTL, SCUT. Turning a light off only hides it on the screen, whether or not the ECU sends it. RPM bar scale : the maximum RPM of the on-screen bar, 1000–20000. RPM shift light : the LED strip above the screen: Light-up RPM , LED brightness , the RPM bar pattern (Mode 1–4), and a Test LEDs button to try it without revving the engine. The RPM shift light settings only appear on dashes that actually have the LED strip.

docs.text: Diagnostik di Mazduino Tuner ¶ Alat diagnostik ada di grup Diagnostics pada menu. Ketik namanya di pencarian menu untuk membukanya dengan cepat. Alat Fungsi Error codes Kode error dan peringatan dari ECU Tune problems Pemeriksaan pengaturan yang tidak wajar Temporary cylinder shutoff Mematikan satu silinder untuk mencari silinder yang lemah Trigger logger Merekam sinyal CKP/CMP dan mengenali pola roda trigger Trigger sniffer Tepi sinyal trigger dan titik TDC seperti yang dilihat firmware Trigger oscilloscope Bentuk tegangan sinyal CKP/CMP (jika didukung ECU) CAN analyzer Melihat lalu lintas CAN lewat ECU Selain itu grup Diagnostics juga berisi halaman tes output dari firmware (injektor, koil, relay, dan lain-lain). Alat yang membebani ECU Trigger logger, trigger sniffer, dan oscilloscope membuat ECU dan USB sibuk. Selama berjalan, status bar menampilkan penandanya. Jika Anda pindah halaman saat alat masih berjalan, aplikasi menanyakan apakah alat dihentikan. Error Codes ¶ Status : OK, no codes jika tidak ada error aktif, beserta jumlah peringatan sejak ECU menyala. Recent codes : kode terakhir dengan keterangannya. Kode P0xxx adalah kode OBD standar; angka lain adalah kode firmware Mazduino. Clear codes menghapus daftar peringatan di ECU, bukan tune. Tune Problems ¶ Memeriksa tune dan menampilkan pengaturan yang tidak wajar atau saling bertentangan, beserta tingkat kepentingannya. Temporary Cylinder Shutoff ¶ Memutus bahan bakar dan pengapian satu silinder untuk mencari silinder yang lemah. Fitur ini hanya ada di Mazduino Tuner. Nyalakan mesin dan biarkan idle stabil. Klik tombol Cylinder N . Tombol berubah menjadi OFF N dengan hitungan mundur, dan di bawahnya tampil berapa RPM turun. Bandingkan penurunan RPM tiap silinder: RPM turun banyak = silinder sehat. RPM hampir tidak turun = silinder bermasalah (injektor, busi/koil, kompresi). Klik lagi tombol yang sama untuk menyalakan silinder itu, atau Restore all untuk semua. Lebih dari satu silinder bisa dimatikan bersamaan, tapi minimal satu silinder tetap menyala. Silinder menyala kembali sendiri: 10 detik setelah perintah terakhir . Setiap silinder yang dimatikan memulai ulang hitungan ini, lalu semua silinder menyala lagi bersamaan. Saat halaman ditutup. Saat injection mode diubah dari sequential. Syarat: Allow writes aktif. Mesin menyala. Injection mode = Sequential . Pada mode batch atau simultaneous, satu injektor juga mengisi silinder lain, jadi fitur ini ditolak. Firmware Mazduino Nightly 4 November 2026 atau lebih baru. Pada firmware yang lebih lama, tombol tidak aktif. Trigger Logger ¶ Merekam sinyal CKP (primary), CMP (cam), sync , dan TDC saat cranking atau mesin menyala, lalu mengenali pola roda trigger dari waktu antar gigi. Gigi yang hilang (missing tooth) tampil sebagai batang tinggi berwarna oranye. Klik Start , lalu crank atau nyalakan mesin. Lihat Detected wheel dan bandingkan dengan Trigger setting . Jika berbeda, aplikasi memberi peringatan untuk memeriksa pengaturan trigger atau sensor. Save CSV menyimpan rekaman; Clear menghapusnya. Centang CKP teeth only (tooth logger) untuk merekam gigi CKP saja. ECU mengirim rekaman per buffer. Jeda waktu di antara dua buffer tidak terekam, jadi digambar pendek dengan garis tipis vertikal sebagai penanda. Garis itu bukan berarti sinyal hilang. Trigger Sniffer ¶ Menampilkan tepi sinyal CKP dan CMP serta titik TDC seperti yang dilihat firmware (engine sniffer), dengan RPM setiap siklus. Bisa dipakai di semua board Mazduino kecuali varian BIGFUEL , yang tidak punya engine sniffer. Klik Start . Setiap siklus mesin yang diterima menambah Charts received . Garis oranye TDC menandai titik mati atas silinder 1 beserta RPM saat itu. Batang di bawah adalah waktu antar gigi; batang oranye adalah gigi yang hilang. Bandingkan Detected wheel dengan Trigger setting , dan perhatikan Trigger errors . Firmware hanya merekam di bawah batas RPM engine sniffer. Jika RPM di atas batas itu, halaman ini memberi tahu Anda. Trigger Oscilloscope ¶ Menampilkan bentuk sinyal analog (tegangan) input CKP/CMP dari ADC ECU, untuk memeriksa sensor VR/hall, noise, dan level tegangan. Halaman ini hanya muncul jika hardware dan firmware ECU mendukungnya. CAN Analyzer ¶ Menampilkan lalu lintas CAN lewat controller ECU sendiri, tanpa adapter tambahan. Start menyalakan pencetakan CAN di RAM ECU saja. Pengaturan ini tidak disimpan ke flash dan dikembalikan saat Stop , saat halaman ditutup, atau sebelum Burn. Mode ini untuk bus yang sepi. Di bus yang ramai sebagian frame bisa hilang. Waktu frame adalah saat data tiba di PC, jadi perkiraan. Untuk menyadap jaringan mobil pabrikan, nyalakan dulu Listen mode di pengaturan CAN agar ECU tidak mengganggu bus. Jika CAN read di tune mati, frame masuk tidak akan terlihat.
docs.title: Diagnostics

docs.text: Koneksi dan Tampilan Mazduino Tuner ¶ Halaman ini menjelaskan cara menghubungkan ECU dan bagian-bagian tampilan Mazduino Tuner. Menghubungkan ECU ¶ Colokkan ECU ke USB. Pilih port di toolbar (misalnya COM5 ). Klik Connect . Saat terhubung, status bar di kiri bawah menampilkan Connected · COM5 dan ECU OK . Klik Disconnect untuk melepas. Saat disconnect atau aplikasi ditutup, port serial benar-benar dilepas sehingga bisa dipakai aplikasi lain. Auto-connect Aktifkan Auto-connect di Settings agar aplikasi langsung connect ke port terakhir setiap kali ECU dicolok. Bagian-bagian Tampilan ¶ Bagian Letak Fungsi Judul jendela paling atas Versi aplikasi, status koneksi, nama proyek, dan firmware Toolbar atas Open/Save proyek, port, Connect, Allow writes, Send to ECU, Burn, Firmware, Settings Menu kiri Semua halaman pengaturan ECU, dikelompokkan per sistem mesin, dengan pencarian Halaman tengah Pengaturan, tabel, atau kurva dari menu yang dipilih Panel bawah bawah Logger, Real Time, dan Shortcuts Nilai utama di bawah panel RPM, MAP, TPS, AFR, suhu, dan lainnya, selalu terlihat Status bar paling bawah Status koneksi, status burn, pesan terakhir, kecepatan data Judul Jendela ¶ Judul jendela menunjukkan: Versi Mazduino Tuner Status : CONNECTED , CONNECTING , RECONNECTING , OFFLINE (proyek dibuka tanpa ECU), atau DISCONNECTED Nama proyek .mdt yang terbuka. Tanda * berarti ada perubahan yang belum disimpan ke file. FW : board dan tanggal firmware dari tune yang sedang tampil Toolbar ¶ Tombol Fungsi Open Membuka proyek tune .mdt . Bisa diedit tanpa ECU; saat ECU terhubung tune dibandingkan. Save Menyimpan tune ke proyek .mdt . Shift+klik untuk menyimpan sebagai file baru. Port Memilih port USB ECU Connect / Disconnect Menghubungkan atau melepas ECU Allow writes Mengizinkan aplikasi menulis ke ECU (hanya sesi ini) Send to ECU Mengirim perubahan yang tertunda ke RAM ECU Burn Menyimpan isi RAM ECU ke flash agar tetap ada setelah ECU mati Firmware Update firmware ECU. Lihat Update Firmware . Settings Pengaturan aplikasi Di kanan toolbar tertulis board dan versi firmware ECU yang terhubung. Menu dan Pencarian ¶ Menu di kiri dikelompokkan per sistem mesin, misalnya Configuration, Limits, Fuel, Ignition, Idle control, Boost control, VVT, CAN Bus, Inputs, Outputs, Tuning, Diagnostics, dan Expert. Angka di kanan menunjukkan jumlah halaman di dalam grup. Halaman untuk fitur yang tidak aktif disembunyikan. Pengaturan yang jarang dipakai ada di grup Expert . Ketik di kotak Search menu or ID untuk mencari halaman. Hasilnya langsung tersaring: Ikon kecil di depan nama halaman menunjukkan jenisnya: Ikon Jenis D Halaman pengaturan (dialog) T Tabel 2D C Kurva A Halaman aplikasi (Start, diagnostik) Di kanan atas setiap halaman ada ID halaman (misalnya veTableDialog ) yang juga bisa dicari, dan label mode tulis: local edits (perubahan hanya di aplikasi) atau writes allowed . Klik Kanan pada Halaman ¶ Klik kanan sebuah halaman di menu (di layar sentuh: tekan lama): Pilihan Fungsi Load this page from another file... Memuat pengaturan halaman ini saja dari file .mdt atau .msq . Lihat Memuat Satu Halaman dari File . Keyboard shortcut... Memberi halaman ini tombol F2 sampai F12, atau menghapusnya ( No shortcut ). Daftar tombol menunjukkan halaman mana yang sudah memakai tiap tombol; tombol yang dipilih pindah ke halaman ini. Add to Shortcuts / Remove from Shortcuts Menambah atau menghapus halaman dari tab SHORTCUTS Tombol yang dipakai halaman tertulis di samping namanya, misalnya Fuel priming (F8) . Bawaan: F5 Fuel table, F6 target AFR/Lambda, F7 Ignition table, F11 Trigger. Semua bisa diganti. Tab SHORTCUTS ¶ Tab SHORTCUTS di atas menu berisi halaman yang Anda tambahkan, sesuai urutan ditambahkan. Klik untuk membuka, klik kanan untuk menu yang sama seperti di atas. Panel Bawah ¶ Panel bawah berisi tiga tab: Logger , Real Time , dan Shortcuts . Garis pembatas di atas panel bisa ditarik untuk memperbesar atau memperkecil panel. Lihat Logger dan Real Time . Nilai Utama ¶ Baris nilai di bawah panel selalu terlihat. Ada beberapa tab (General Tuning, Idle, Boost, VVT). Klik kanan (atau tekan lama) sebuah nilai untuk menggantinya dengan channel lain. Status Bar ¶ Bagian Arti Connected · COM5 ECU terhubung di port tersebut ECU OK Tidak ada error kritis di ECU Saved to flash Semua perubahan sudah di-burn. Jika belum, tombol Burn ikut menyala. Pesan Pesan terakhir aplikasi, misalnya hasil edit atau burn 50 Hz · 1 ms · 2216 B Kecepatan data live, waktu respons ECU, dan ukuran data per baca INI Sumber file definisi (cache, unduhan, atau file) Halaman Start ¶ Halaman Start menampilkan board, port, dan firmware ECU yang terhubung.
docs.title: Connection and Layout

docs.text: Logger dan Real Time di Mazduino Tuner ¶ Panel bawah Mazduino Tuner berisi tiga tab: Logger , Real Time , dan Shortcuts . Tarik garis pembatas di atas panel untuk mengubah tingginya. Logger ¶ Selama ECU terhubung, semua channel selalu direkam (sekitar 11 menit terakhir pada 50 Hz). Anda tidak perlu menekan tombol rekam. Tombol Fungsi Recording Lama rekaman yang tersimpan saat ini Graph on / Graph off Menyalakan atau mematikan grafik live. Mematikan grafik menghemat CPU; perekaman tetap berjalan. Live / Go live Grafik mengikuti data terbaru. Jika digeser ke belakang, klik Go live untuk kembali. 10 s Lebar rentang waktu yang terlihat Select Klik pada grafik memilih rentang waktu (sama dengan Shift+klik), misalnya untuk menyimpan sebagian log Channels Memilih channel yang digambar Preset Menyimpan dan memakai kumpulan channel, misalnya "Idle" atau "Dyno" Open Membuka file log .mlg atau .csv Save Menyimpan log sebagai .mlg atau .csv Di kanan grafik tertulis nilai setiap channel pada posisi kursor. Simpan otomatis : aktifkan Save when disconnecting di Settings. Log yang lebih dari 30 detik disimpan saat disconnect, di folder Logs di samping proyek .mdt , atau di Documents\Mazduino Tuner\Logs\<nama kendaraan> . Di samping setiap log juga tersimpan tune yang dipakai ECU saat log direkam ( .mdt ). Real Time ¶ Tab Real Time menampilkan nilai live dari channel ECU dalam kolom-kolom, dikelompokkan seperti dashboard. Grup Engine Control (RPM, MAP, TPS, AFR, suhu, timing, injektor) selalu di depan. Klik judul grup untuk membuka atau menutupnya. Scroll mouse menggeser kolom ke samping. Arahkan kursor ke nama channel untuk melihat nama aslinya. Memilih Channel yang Ditampilkan ¶ Di kanan atas tab ada tiga pilihan: Pilihan Yang ditampilkan In use Hanya channel dari fitur yang dipakai ECU (default) All Semua channel My channels Hanya channel pilihan Anda Klik Choose channels... untuk memilih channel sendiri: Ketik di kotak pencarian untuk menyaring, misalnya temp : Centang atau hilangkan centang per channel. Pick shown / Clear shown mencentang atau menghapus semua channel yang sedang tampil. Picked only menampilkan hanya channel yang sudah dicentang. Save menyimpan pilihan dan beralih ke My channels . Kotak Search channels di kanan atas tab Real Time menyaring kolom secara langsung. Shortcuts ¶ Tab Shortcuts berisi daftar tombol keyboard. Klik baris halaman untuk langsung membukanya. Tombol Fungsi F5 / F6 / F7 / F11 (bawaan) Fuel table (VE) / tabel target AFR / Ignition table / Trigger. Bisa diganti dan ditambah (F2 sampai F12) lewat klik kanan halaman di menu. W atau + / Q atau − Naikkan / turunkan sel terpilih (Shift: 10 langkah) = atau Enter Isi semua sel terpilih H / V Interpolasi horizontal / vertikal S Smooth M atau *1.05 Kalikan angka Ketik nilai untuk sel terpilih Space Follow: ikuti sel yang dipakai mesin Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y Undo / Redo Ctrl+S Simpan proyek .mdt Ctrl+B Burn ke flash (perlu Allow writes) Nilai Utama ¶ Baris nilai di bawah panel (RPM, MAP, Throttle position, AFR, Coolant temp, dan lainnya) selalu terlihat. Gunakan tab General Tuning , Idle , Boost , VVT untuk set nilai lain. Klik kanan (atau tekan lama) sebuah nilai untuk menggantinya dengan channel lain.

docs.text: Manual Mazduino Tuner ¶ Mazduino Tuner adalah software tuning resmi untuk ECU Mazduino berbasis rusEFI. Software ini membaca definisi (INI) langsung dari firmware di ECU, jadi semua menu dan halaman selalu cocok dengan firmware yang terpasang. Firmware ECU juga bisa diupdate langsung dari aplikasi. Versi alpha Mazduino Tuner masih dalam tahap pengujian (alpha). Simpan selalu salinan tune Anda ( .mdt atau .msq ) sebelum menulis ke ECU, dan jangan mengandalkannya untuk mesin yang tidak boleh bermasalah. Isi Manual ¶ Halaman Isi Instalasi Unduh, pasang, dan jalankan pertama kali Koneksi dan Tampilan Menghubungkan ECU, toolbar, menu, panel bawah, status Mengubah Tune Halaman pengaturan, tabel dan kurva, Allow writes, Send, Burn Proyek dan File Tune Proyek .mdt , edit offline, tune laptop vs ECU, file .msq Update Firmware Update firmware ECU lewat USB dan memeriksa tune setelahnya Logger dan Real Time Data log, grafik, daftar channel, shortcut Diagnostik Error code, trigger logger, sniffer, CAN analyzer, tes silinder Kebutuhan Sistem ¶ Sistem operasi : Windows 10 atau 11 (64-bit) Koneksi : port USB untuk ECU Mazduino Hak administrator : tidak perlu untuk instalasi. Windows hanya meminta izin sekali saat driver USB bootloader dipasang (untuk update firmware). Mazduino Tuner dibuat untuk ECU Mazduino dengan firmware Mazduino (rusEFI). Board rusEFI lain dan Speeduino juga bisa dibuka. Instalasi ¶ Langkah 1: Unduh installer ¶ Buka halaman Releases Mazduino Tuner dan unduh file MazduinoTuner-Setup-<versi>.exe dari rilis terbaru. Langkah 2: Jalankan installer ¶ Klik dua kali file installer. Versi alpha belum ditandatangani (code signing), jadi Windows SmartScreen bisa menampilkan "Windows protected your PC" . Klik More info , lalu Run anyway . Pastikan file memang diunduh dari halaman Releases di atas. Ikuti langkah installer. Aplikasi dipasang untuk user yang sedang login, tanpa hak administrator. Di akhir instalasi Windows bisa menanyakan izin untuk memasang driver USB bootloader STM32 . Driver ini dipakai saat update firmware. Setujui; kalau dilewati, aplikasi akan memintanya lagi saat pertama kali update firmware. Langkah 3: Jalankan pertama kali ¶ Buka Mazduino Tuner dari Start Menu atau shortcut desktop. Hubungkan ECU dengan kabel USB. Pilih port ECU (misalnya COM5 ) di toolbar, lalu klik Connect . Aplikasi membaca signature firmware, mengambil file INI yang cocok, lalu membuka menu sesuai board dan firmware. Lihat Koneksi dan Tampilan . File INI tidak perlu dipilih manual Untuk firmware Mazduino, INI diunduh otomatis sesuai signature dan disimpan di cache, jadi berikutnya tidak perlu internet lagi. INI juga ikut tersimpan di setiap proyek .mdt . Hanya untuk firmware yang tidak dikenal aplikasi akan meminta Anda memilih file INI sekali. Pengaturan Aplikasi ¶ Klik Settings di kanan atas. Pengaturan Keterangan Theme System, Dark, atau Light Language Bahasa Indonesia atau English Temperature / Pressure / Mixture Satuan tampilan (°C/°F, kPa/psi, Lambda/AFR). Hanya tampilan; isi ECU tidak berubah. Data rate Berapa kali per detik data live dibaca (10, 20, 50, 100). Default 50, maksimal 100 agar ECU tidak terbebani. Auto-connect Langsung connect ke port terakhir saat ECU dicolok Import / Export / Compare .msq Bertukar tune dengan TunerStudio. Lihat Proyek dan File Tune . Save when disconnecting Simpan data log otomatis saat disconnect Log folder Membuka folder data log Lokasi File ¶ Isi Lokasi Pengaturan aplikasi, log koneksi dan update firmware, backup tune sebelum update %APPDATA%\MazduinoTuner Data log Documents\Mazduino Tuner\Logs , atau folder Logs di samping proyek .mdt Uninstall tidak menghapus folder-folder ini. Melaporkan Masalah ¶ Buat laporan di halaman Issues dengan menyertakan: versi Mazduino Tuner (terlihat di judul jendela) dan firmware ECU (di kanan atas toolbar) langkah yang dilakukan dan apa yang terjadi %APPDATA%\MazduinoTuner\connection.log untuk masalah koneksi, atau %APPDATA%\MazduinoTuner\firmware-update.log untuk masalah update firmware

docs.text: Proyek dan File Tune di Mazduino Tuner ¶ Mazduino Tuner menyimpan tune dalam proyek .mdt . Untuk bertukar tune dengan TunerStudio, aplikasi juga bisa membuka, menyimpan, dan membandingkan file .msq . Proyek .mdt ¶ File .mdt menyimpan: semua nilai tune persis seperti di ECU (tanpa pembulatan) signature firmware tempat tune itu dibuat definisi firmware (INI), sehingga proyek bisa dibuka di komputer mana pun tanpa internet Menyimpan Proyek ¶ Klik Save di toolbar (atau Ctrl+S). Pertama kali, pilih folder dan nama file, misalnya Lancer-Evo.mdt . Berikutnya Save langsung menimpa file yang sama. Shift+klik Save untuk menyimpan sebagai file baru. Nama proyek tampil di judul jendela. Tanda * berarti ada perubahan yang belum disimpan. Membuka dan Mengedit Proyek Tanpa ECU ¶ Klik Open , pilih file .mdt . Tanpa ECU, proyek terbuka OFFLINE dan semua halaman bisa dilihat dan diedit seperti biasa: Jangan lupa Save setelah mengedit. Tune di Mazduino Tuner Berbeda dengan ECU ¶ Saat ECU dihubungkan dan proyek sedang terbuka, aplikasi membandingkan tune proyek dengan tune di ECU. Jika berbeda, muncul dialog berikut. Data live dan penulisan ke ECU ditahan sampai Anda memilih. Isi dialog: Daftar kiri : setiap pengaturan yang berbeda dengan nama dan letaknya di menu, misalnya VE Table — Tuning > Fuel table — 1 of 256 cells . Detail kanan : Tabel : grid dengan sel yang berbeda diberi kotak oranye. Pilih Show ECU atau Show Mazduino Tuner untuk melihat nilai dari masing-masing sisi. Di bawahnya ada daftar sel yang berbeda: posisi (RPM, beban), nilai ECU, nilai Mazduino Tuner, dan selisihnya. Kurva : semua titik dengan baris yang berbeda ditandai. Nilai tunggal : nilai ECU dan nilai Mazduino Tuner berdampingan. Pilihan : Use the ECU tune — tune di Mazduino Tuner diganti dengan isi ECU. Tidak ada yang ditulis ke ECU. Send the Mazduino Tuner tune to the ECU — tune proyek ditulis ke ECU lalu di-burn. Pengaturan internal firmware yang tidak ada di menu (misalnya tanggal build firmware) tidak ditampilkan di daftar, hanya disebut jumlahnya. Jika hanya itu yang berbeda, dialog tidak muncul. Proyek dari Firmware Lain ¶ Setiap update firmware rusEFI bisa memindahkan posisi pengaturan di memori ECU. Jika tune lama disalin mentah ke firmware baru, nilainya bisa masuk ke pengaturan yang salah tanpa terlihat. Karena itu Mazduino Tuner memindahkan tune berdasarkan nama pengaturan , dan hanya jika aman: Proyek dibuat dengan ECU memakai Yang terjadi Firmware sama Firmware sama Dibandingkan langsung Mazduino, board sama, tanggal lain (misalnya mazduino-lite 2026-08-17) Mazduino, board sama (misalnya mazduino-lite 2026-11-08) Dibandingkan dan dikirim berdasarkan nama ; aman walau posisinya bergeser Board lain, epicEFI, rusEFI official, atau firmware lain Firmware Mazduino Peringatan : tune lama tidak bisa dipakai, samakan secara manual Untuk firmware yang berbeda, daftar perbedaan tetap ditampilkan sebagai panduan untuk menyamakan nilai secara manual, tetapi hanya ada pilihan Use the ECU tune . File proyeknya tidak diubah. Banyak Mazduino Lite memakai firmware rusEFI f407-discovery ECU Mazduino Lite yang sebelumnya memakai firmware rusEFI f407-discovery termasuk "firmware lain" saat dipindah ke firmware Mazduino mazduino-lite . Simpan tune lama sebagai .msq , lalu samakan pengaturan secara manual dengan bantuan Compare . File TunerStudio ( .msq ) ¶ Buka Settings , bagian TunerStudio tune file (.msq) : Tombol Fungsi Import Memuat file .msq ke tune lokal. Belum dikirim ke ECU; bisa dibatalkan dengan Undo. Export Menyimpan tune lokal sebagai .msq (termasuk perubahan yang belum dikirim) Compare Membandingkan tune lokal dengan file .msq Nilai dicocokkan berdasarkan nama pengaturan. Jika signature file berbeda tetapi masih firmware Mazduino dengan board yang sama, aplikasi meminta konfirmasi dulu: Hasil Compare memakai tampilan yang sama dengan dialog di atas: Close — tune lokal tidak diubah. Apply the file to the local tune — nilai dari file diterapkan ke tune lokal. Belum dikirim ke ECU; kirim dengan Send to ECU dan simpan dengan Burn . Untuk file dari firmware lain, Import ditolak dengan peringatan, sedangkan Compare tetap bisa dipakai sebagai panduan (tanpa tombol Apply). Memuat Satu Halaman dari File ¶ Untuk mengambil pengaturan satu halaman saja dari tune lain (misalnya cranking dari tune mobil lain), klik kanan halaman itu di menu, lalu pilih Load this page from another file... dan pilih file .mdt atau .msq . Hanya pengaturan di halaman itu yang dibandingkan, dengan tampilan yang sama seperti di atas. Apply to this page menerapkan nilai dari file ke tune lokal. Belum dikirim ke ECU: kirim dengan Send to ECU dan simpan dengan Burn , atau batalkan dengan Ctrl+Z . Aturan firmware yang sama berlaku: file dari firmware lain hanya ditampilkan sebagai panduan.

docs.text: Mengubah Tune di Mazduino Tuner ¶ Halaman ini menjelaskan cara mengubah pengaturan, tabel, dan kurva, lalu mengirim dan menyimpan perubahan ke ECU. Alur Perubahan: Lokal, RAM ECU, Flash ¶ Setiap perubahan melewati tiga tahap: Lokal — perubahan baru ada di aplikasi. Sel yang berubah diberi garis putus-putus , dan tertulis jumlah sel yang belum dikirim. RAM ECU — perubahan dikirim ke ECU dan langsung dipakai mesin, tetapi hilang jika ECU mati. Flash — perubahan disimpan permanen dengan Burn . Secara default aplikasi tidak boleh menulis ke ECU. Selama itu, semua edit hanya lokal dan aman untuk dicoba. Pada contoh di atas sembilan sel dinaikkan. Sel-selnya bergaris putus-putus, tertulis 9 cells not sent , dan tombol Send to ECU (15 B) menyala. Klik Undo (Ctrl+Z) untuk membatalkan. Allow writes ¶ Klik Allow writes di toolbar untuk mengizinkan aplikasi menulis ke ECU. Aplikasi meminta konfirmasi: Setelah diizinkan, tombol berwarna oranye dan label halaman berubah menjadi writes allowed : Selama Allow writes aktif: Setiap edit langsung dikirim ke RAM ECU dan langsung dipakai mesin. Send to ECU mengirim perubahan yang tertunda (misalnya yang dibuat sebelum Allow writes dinyalakan). Burn (Ctrl+B) menyimpan ke flash. Status bar menampilkan Saved to flash jika semua sudah tersimpan. Izin ini hanya berlaku sampai disconnect. Klik Allow writes lagi untuk mematikannya. Perhatikan kondisi mesin Dengan Allow writes aktif, perubahan langsung dipakai mesin. Pastikan Anda memahami nilai yang diubah, terutama saat mesin menyala. Halaman Pengaturan ¶ Halaman pengaturan (ikon D di menu) berisi kolom isian, pilihan, dan catatan dari firmware. Contoh halaman Trigger (tombol F11): Kolom angka menampilkan satuan dan batas nilai, misalnya deg btdc [-720 – 720] . Teks oranye adalah catatan penting dari firmware. Kolom abu-abu sedang tidak berlaku untuk pengaturan saat ini (misalnya Secondary channel saat tidak ada sensor kedua). Tombol Help membuka penjelasan halaman. Tabel ¶ Contoh halaman Fuel table (F5) dengan VE Table : Sumbu X di atas (biasanya RPM) dan sumbu Y di kiri (beban: MAP, TPS, dan lain-lain, sesuai mode). Warna sel menunjukkan besar kecilnya nilai. Memilih sel : klik sel, atau klik lalu tarik untuk memilih blok. Tombol Keyboard Fungsi − / + Q / W (atau − / +) Turunkan / naikkan sel terpilih satu langkah. Dengan Shift: 10 langkah. H / V H / V Interpolasi horizontal / vertikal di antara sel tepi S S Smooth (haluskan) blok terpilih = = / Enter Isi semua sel terpilih dengan satu nilai × M Kalikan sel terpilih (misalnya *1.05 = +5%) angka ketik angka Ketik nilai untuk sel terpilih Follow Space Pilihan mengikuti sel yang sedang dipakai mesin (RPM × beban) AT Panel VE autotune Undo / Redo Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y Batalkan / ulangi perubahan i Tampilkan ringkasan tombol dan shortcut tabel Saat ECU terhubung, sel yang sedang dipakai mesin ditandai di tabel. VE Autotune ¶ Tombol AT di tabel VE membuka panel autotune. Panel ini mengusulkan koreksi VE dari lambda terukur dibanding target, sel per sel. Ctrl+T menerapkan koreksi pada sel di posisi mesin. Jika Allow writes mati, koreksi hanya mengubah tune lokal dan bisa dikirim ke ECU nanti. Saat autotune berjalan, status bar menampilkan penandanya. Kurva ¶ Kurva (ikon C di menu) berupa satu baris nilai dengan sumbunya di bawah. Contoh Warmup enrichment : Klik atau tarik untuk memilih titik, lalu pakai − , + , atau = seperti pada tabel. Klik dua kali angka sumbu untuk mengubah titik sumbu. Shortcut Halaman ¶ Tombol (bawaan) Halaman F5 Fuel table (VE) F6 Tabel target AFR / Lambda F7 Ignition table F11 Trigger Tombol F2 sampai F12 bisa diberikan ke halaman mana pun lewat klik kanan di menu. Lihat Klik Kanan pada Halaman . Daftar lengkap ada di tab Shortcuts di panel bawah ( Logger dan Real Time ).
